402: ## 12. Security
403: 
404: | ID | Requirement |
405: | --- | --- |
406: | **SEC1 Passwords** | Argon2id; 12 to 128 characters; never stored, logged or returned in plaintext. |
407: | **SEC2 Sessions** | Server-side revocable sessions in an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie, `Secure` over TLS. |
408: | **SEC3 CSRF** | A CSRF token on every non-GET request. |
409: | **SEC4 Authorisation** | Role and ownership checked in every service and repository call; foreign resources return 404; generated role-matrix and ownership tests. |
410: | **SEC5 Authentication errors** | Identical responses for unknown email and wrong password; a dummy hash is checked so timing does not reveal accounts. |
411: | **SEC6 Rate limiting** | Failed logins (5 per account and per IP in 15 minutes), browsing, claim creation and handover attempts. |
412: | **SEC7 TLS for credentials** | Credentials only over TLS beyond localhost; forwarded headers trusted only from the configured proxy. |
413: | **SEC8 Input and uploads** | Strict schemas, forbidden unknown fields, size limits, content-based file type checks, decompression guards, parameterised queries. |
414: | **SEC9 Headers and CORS** | Content-Security-Policy, `nosniff`, referrer policy, frame protection, CORS limited to the configured origin; user text is always escaped. |
415: | **SEC10 Secrets** | Only in environment variables; no `.env` in the repository; production mode refuses placeholders. |
416: | **SEC11 Dependencies** | `pip-audit` and `npm audit` before release. |
417: | **SEC12 Logging** | Structured logs with request IDs and no passwords, tokens, codes or full emails. |

419: ## 13. Production Deployment
420: 
421: The project must run as a deployed service. "Deployed" means: built into container images and run as long-lived services that you open in a browser on your own computer or from another device on the same network (intranet). It handles personal reports, photos and claim evidence, so credentials must not cross a network in the clear.
422: 
423: | ID | Requirement |
424: | --- | --- |
425: | **D1 Services** | Docker Compose runs `db` (PostgreSQL with pgvector and a named volume), `backend` (FastAPI under a production server), `worker` (same code and models), `frontend` (built files behind nginx, proxying `/api`), and a mail catcher for development. |
426: | **D2 Non-root, pinned** | Application containers run as a non-root user; images and dependencies are pinned. |
427: | **D3 One command** | After `cp .env.example .env` and setting the secrets, `docker compose up -d` builds and starts everything, applies migrations, and serves the UI at `http://localhost:8080`. |
428: | **D4 Offline models** | Model weights are fetched at build time with pinned revisions and checksums and baked into the images; the running backend and worker need no outbound network access. |
429: | **D5 Health and restart** | `/api/health` reports the database and worker status; all services have health checks and `restart: unless-stopped`. |
430: | **D6 Persistence and backup** | Named volumes for the database and the images, and a documented backup and restore of both, verified by restoring into a clean setup. |
431: | **D7 HTTPS on the network** | A TLS reverse proxy serves `https://<LAN-IP>:8443` with a certificate from a private certificate authority you create (a tool such as mkcert can do this) that your devices trust; plain-HTTP credentials from non-localhost clients are refused. |
432: | **D8 Email** | The development mail catcher shows every email; production uses an SMTP server set in the environment. Deliverability from a self-hosted server is a documented limitation. |
433: | **D9 Seed and demo data** | A command loads a synthetic campus tree and a demo dataset with one account per role, all labelled synthetic. |
434: | **D10 Optional public host** | A public deployment is optional and uses synthetic data only. |

461: ## 15. Acceptance Criteria
462: 
463: Clocks in tests are injected, so results are deterministic.
464: 
465: ### Accounts, roles and security
466: - [ ] **AC-01** (FR-01) Registering with an email outside `ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS` returns 422 `email_domain_not_allowed`; an allowed email creates an unverified account, stores an Argon2id hash (the stored value starts with `$argon2id$`), never returns or logs the password, and a duplicate email (compared case-insensitively) returns 409.
467: - [ ] **AC-02** (FR-01) An unverified account cannot create reports or claims (403 `email_not_verified`). The emailed verification link works once, expires after 24 hours (injected clock), and a reused or expired link returns 410.
468: - [ ] **AC-03** (SEC1) Passwords of 11 characters are rejected with 422; 12 and 128 are accepted; 129 is rejected.
469: - [ ] **AC-04** (SEC2, SEC5, SEC6) Login sets an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie (and `Secure` over TLS); a wrong email and a wrong password return identical responses; the 6th failed login for one account within 15 minutes returns 429 with `Retry-After`.
470: - [ ] **AC-05** (SEC2) After logout or account deletion, the old session cookie returns 401 on every endpoint.
471: - [ ] **AC-06** (SEC3) A POST, PATCH or DELETE without a valid CSRF token returns 403 `csrf_failed`; GET requests are unaffected.
472: - [ ] **AC-07** (SEC7) A login over plain HTTP from a non-localhost client returns 403 `tls_required`; over TLS or from localhost it works; a forged forwarded-protocol header from an untrusted client is ignored.
473: - [ ] **AC-08** (SEC4) *Role matrix.* A generated test calls every route as anonymous, user, moderator and admin, and checks each response against the access matrix of section 3; no role ever receives more access than the matrix allows.
474: - [ ] **AC-09** (SEC4) User B requesting, changing or deleting user A's report, claim, evidence image, notification or handover by ID gets a 404 identical to a missing ID, and A's data is unchanged.
475: - [ ] **AC-10** (SEC8) A request body containing an unknown field, including `reporter_id` or `claimant_id`, is rejected with 422.
476: - [ ] **AC-11** (SEC8) The string `'; DROP TABLE users;--` saved in a description is stored and returned literally, and all tables remain intact.
477: - [ ] **AC-12** (SEC8, SEC9) A description containing `<script>alert(1)</script>` is stored as text and rendered escaped; an end-to-end test confirms no script runs, and the Content-Security-Policy header is present.
478: - [ ] **AC-13** (SEC9) Responses carry the Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy` and frame-protection headers; CORS allows only the configured origin.
479: - [ ] **AC-14** (SEC10) A script finds no secret patterns in tracked files and no tracked `.env`; in production mode the application refuses to start with a missing secret or one equal to the `.env.example` placeholder.
480: - [ ] **AC-15** (SEC8) A non-upload request body above 1 MB returns 413.
481: - [ ] **AC-16** (SEC11) `pip-audit` and `npm audit` show no known high or critical vulnerabilities at release; the results are recorded.
482: 
483: ### Campus locations
484: - [ ] **AC-17** (FR-02) An admin can build a location tree (campus, building, floor, room or area). A node cannot become its own ancestor (422), sibling names are unique (case-insensitive), and deleting a location that reports use returns 409.
485: - [ ] **AC-18** (6.3) *Location score.* In a tree of Main Campus, Library (floors 1 and 2; floor 2 has Reading Room and Study Pod), Student Center and Gym, with Library and Student Center adjacent: Reading Room against Reading Room scores **1.0**; Library against Reading Room **0.8**; Reading Room against Study Pod **0.7**; Reading Room against Floor 1 **0.6**; Library against Student Center **0.5**; Library against Gym **0.2**; a location in another campus **0.0**; a missing location gives `null`.
486: - [ ] **AC-19** (FR-02) Adjacency is symmetric: adding Library to Student Center makes both directions score 0.5, and removing it returns the pair to 0.2.
487: - [ ] **AC-20** (FR-02) A report can use a location at any level (building-level is allowed), no GPS is ever required, and optional coordinates are stored rounded to 3 decimal places.
488: 
489: ### Reports, lifecycle and uploads
490: - [ ] **AC-21** (FR-03) A lost report requires a title (3 to 120 characters), a description (10 to 2,000), a category, a lost-time window and a location; validation errors list each failing field; saving returns without waiting for embeddings.
491: - [ ] **AC-22** (FR-04) A found report requires the same fields plus a found time; it may add private details (up to 1,000 characters) and up to 3 verification prompts (each up to 200 characters). With moderation on (default), it starts as `pending_review` and is not listed until approved.
492: - [ ] **AC-23** (5.2) For the timezone `Asia/Kolkata`, a `day` precision on 2026-10-15 gives the window 2026-10-14T18:30:00Z to 2026-10-15T18:29:59.999Z; `morning` is 06:00 to 12:00 local, `afternoon` 12:00 to 17:00, `evening` 17:00 to 22:00, `night` 22:00 to 06:00 (crossing midnight); `exact` is a zero-length window.
493: - [ ] **AC-24** (FR-03) A category outside the fixed list returns 422.
494: - [ ] **AC-25** (5.1) *Found-report lifecycle.* Every legal transition in the table of section 5.1 succeeds, and every other (state, action) pair returns 409 `invalid_transition` and leaves the report unchanged (tested exhaustively).
495: - [ ] **AC-26** (5.1) The same exhaustive check passes for the lost-report lifecycle.
496: - [ ] **AC-27** (FR-07) A reporter can close their own report; closing someone else's returns 404; a `returned` found report can never reopen.
497: - [ ] **AC-28** (5.6) *PII scanner.* `4111 1111 1111 1111` is flagged `card_number` (it passes the Luhn check); `4111 1111 1111 1112` fails Luhn and is flagged `long_number` (16 digits); `1234 5678 9012` is flagged `long_number`; `+91 98765 43210` is flagged `phone`; `a.b@campus.edu` is flagged `email`; `blue bottle with a RIA sticker` is not flagged.
498: - [ ] **AC-29** (5.6) Public fields (title, description) containing a flagged pattern are rejected with 422 `pii_detected` that names the kind but does not echo the value; private details may contain such text and show a warning only.
499: - [ ] **AC-30** (S4) For the sensitive categories (`id_card`, `wallet`), images are marked non-public automatically, whatever the moderator does, and the public listing shows a placeholder.
500: - [ ] **AC-31** (5.7) Upload type is decided by the file's content, not its name: a PNG named `.jpg` is accepted as PNG; a text file named `.jpg` returns 415; SVG and GIF return 415; JPEG, PNG and WebP are accepted.
501: - [ ] **AC-32** (5.7) A file of 5 MB is accepted and one byte over returns 413; an image above 6,000 × 6,000 pixels returns 422 `image_too_large` before it is fully decoded.
502: - [ ] **AC-33** (5.7) A test image carrying GPS and camera EXIF data has none of it after processing; images are re-encoded, resized to at most 1,600 pixels on the long side, and a thumbnail is created.
503: - [ ] **AC-34** (5.7) Stored files use random UUID keys; the original file name is neither stored nor served.
504: - [ ] **AC-35** (5.7) Images are served only through an authorised route that checks visibility: a private image returns 404 to other users, public images require a login, and responses carry the correct content type and `nosniff`.
505: - [ ] **AC-36** (5.7) A fourth image on one report returns 422.
506: - [ ] **AC-37** (5.7) A 64-bit difference hash is stored per image: an identical image has Hamming distance 0 and a resized copy at most 4 from the original, while an unrelated image has more than 10; a found image whose distance to an image on another user's found report is at most 4 is flagged `duplicate_image` for moderators.
507: 
508: ### Browsing, search and public views
509: - [ ] **AC-38** (FR-06) The found-item listing shows only `open` items. It excludes `pending_review`, `removed`, `returned` and archived items, and shows building-level location, category, public description, date and the public photo.
510: - [ ] **AC-39** (P1) *Default-deny contract test.* Every public serialiser is checked against an explicit whitelist: the listing and detail responses never contain private details, verification prompts, reporter identity, locations finer than building level, private images, or any column added later without being whitelisted.
511: - [ ] **AC-40** (P1) Lost reports are visible only to their reporter, moderators and admins.
512: - [ ] **AC-41** (FR-06) Search matches title and description (PostgreSQL full-text), filters by category, by building (including all descendants) and by date range, combines filters with AND, and paginates with a stable cursor.
513: - [ ] **AC-42** (FR-12) Moderators and admins see full details, including private fields and exact locations.
514: - [ ] **AC-43** (P5) The browse endpoints are rate-limited per user (120 requests per minute, *initial*) and return 429 with `Retry-After` beyond it.
515: - [ ] **AC-44** (P5) Listing and detail require a login (campus users only), and all IDs are unguessable UUIDs.
516: 
517: ### Background jobs and embeddings
518: - [ ] **AC-45** (FR-08) Saving a report enqueues its embedding jobs and returns; *(initial target)* the create-report endpoint takes at most **300 ms at p95** with the models switched off.
519: - [ ] **AC-46** (FR-08) With 2 workers and 1,000 jobs, every job completes exactly once (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`).
520: - [ ] **AC-47** (FR-08) A failing job retries after 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes (injected clock), then becomes `failed` after 5 attempts and appears on the admin page; a manual retry works.
521: - [ ] **AC-48** (FR-08) Running the embedding job again for the same entity and model version leaves exactly one embedding row.
522: - [ ] **AC-49** (6.1) Embeddings record model name, model version and dimension. Matching compares only vectors of the same version; changing the configured version triggers a backfill, and matches computed with the old version are marked stale.
523: - [ ] **AC-50** (6.1) The database rejects a vector of the wrong dimension.
524: 
525: ### Matching and explanations
526: - [ ] **AC-51** (6.2) The text score is `max(0, cosine)` of normalised embeddings: a cosine of 0.82 gives **0.82** and −0.10 gives **0**.
527: - [ ] **AC-52** (6.3) *Time score.* Overlapping windows score **1.0**; a found time 12 hours after the lost window ends scores **0.7788**, and 48 hours after scores **0.3679**; a found time 12 hours before the lost window starts scores **0.1353**, and 6 hours before scores **0.3679**.
528: - [ ] **AC-53** (6.4) *Hybrid example.* With weights text 0.40, image 0.35, location 0.15, time 0.10 and signals 0.8, 0.6, 0.7, 0.5, the score is **0.685**. With the image signal missing, the weights renormalise over 0.65 and the score is **0.7308**.
529: - [ ] **AC-54** (6.4) Missing signals are excluded, never counted as zero: a pair with only a text signal scores exactly its text score.
530: - [ ] **AC-55** (6.2) The image signal uses image-to-image similarity when both reports have photos, text-to-image similarity (the lost text against the found photo, or the reverse) when exactly one does, and `null` when neither does; the explanation names which was used.
531: - [ ] **AC-56** (6.5) Candidates are only lost-to-found pairs where both reports are `open`, the reporters differ, the pair was not dismissed, the found item is not reserved or returned, and the found time lies between 6 hours before the lost window starts and 30 days after it ends; each exclusion has its own fixture test.
532: - [ ] **AC-57** (6.5) Candidates are ordered by score descending, then older found report first, then ID, identically across runs.
533: - [ ] **AC-58** (FR-09) The matches endpoint returns at most 10 candidates (a parameter, maximum 50) with score, bin, signal scores and explanation, and never includes a found report's private fields.
534: - [ ] **AC-59** (6.6) Explanation contributions sum exactly to the combined score (within 1e-9); the explanation lists signals contributing at least 10% of the score, or the top 3; and for the example of AC-53 without an image the contributions are text 0.4923, location 0.1615, time 0.0769.
535: - [ ] **AC-60** (P1) A canary string placed in a found report's private details never appears in any explanation, match response, notification or log.
536: - [ ] **AC-61** (FR-09) Dismissing a match removes the pair permanently for that user and records the feedback; it never reappears after a recompute.
537: - [ ] **AC-62** (S1) No code path changes a report or claim status because of a score: setting a pair's score to 0.99 changes no status, and the UI and API label scores as suggestions.
538: - [ ] **AC-63** (6.5) A new found report triggers scoring against open lost reports, and a new lost report against open found reports; each (lost, found, model version, weights version) is scored once and recomputing is idempotent.
539: - [ ] **AC-64** (6.4) Each stored candidate records its weights version and model versions; changing the weights creates a new version and does not overwrite earlier results.
540: - [ ] **AC-65** (6.4) Scores of at least 0.75 are `high`, at least 0.55 are `medium`, and the rest `low`; a match notification is created only for a score of at least 0.65 ranked in the top 3 (*initial*).
541: - [ ] **AC-66** (6.5) *(initial target)* On 10,000 vectors, the HNSW index returns at least **95%** of the exact top-10 results (recall@10 against exact search).
542: - [ ] **AC-67** (6.5) *(initial targets)* Retrieving and scoring the top 10 for one lost report against 10,000 found reports takes at most **200 ms at p50 and 800 ms at p95**, excluding embedding time.
543: 
544: ### Notifications
545: - [ ] **AC-68** (FR-10) A notification row is written in the same transaction as the state change that causes it; if the transaction rolls back, no notification exists.
546: - [ ] **AC-69** (FR-10) Processing the same event twice creates one notification (a unique event key); an email retried after a crash carries the same `Message-ID`, so duplicates are recognisable.
547: - [ ] **AC-70** (FR-10) An SMTP failure is retried with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts, then marked `failed`.
548: - [ ] **AC-71** (P1) Match and claim emails contain no private details or claim evidence; the handover code appears only in the email and in-app message to the approved claimant.
549: - [ ] **AC-72** (FR-10) Opting out of match emails stops them but not claim or handover emails; in-app notifications still appear.

200: Each signal is a number in [0, 1] or `null` when it cannot be computed.
201: 
202: | Signal | Definition |
203: | --- | --- |
204: | Text | `max(0, cosine)` between the text embeddings of `category + title + description` |
205: | Image | Image-to-image `max(0, cosine)` when both reports have photos (the best pair of photos); otherwise text-to-image `max(0, cosine)` (a report's text against the other report's photo) when exactly one has photos; otherwise `null` |
206: | Location | The table in 6.3 |
207: | Time | The decay function in 6.3 |
208: 
209: ### 6.3 Location and time scores
210: 
211: **Location score** by the relationship between the two locations in the tree:
212: 
213: | Relationship | Score |
214: | --- | --- |
215: | Identical | 1.0 |
216: | One is an ancestor of the other | 0.8 |
217: | Share a floor or an area (lowest common ancestor is a floor or an area) | 0.7 |
218: | Share a building only | 0.6 |
219: | Different buildings that are adjacent | 0.5 |
220: | Same campus, not adjacent | 0.2 |
221: | Different campuses | 0.0 |
222: | A location is missing | `null` |
223: 
224: **Time score** compares the two windows. If they overlap, the score is 1. Otherwise let `gap` be the hours between them: if the found window is after the lost window, `score = exp(−gap / 48)`; if it is before, `score = exp(−gap / 6)`. The asymmetry reflects that a finder cannot find something before it was lost, apart from imprecise reporting.
225: 
226: ### 6.4 Hybrid score
227: 
228: `score = Σ wᵢ sᵢ / Σ wᵢ`, summed **only over signals that are not `null`**. Initial weights: text 0.40, image 0.35, location 0.15, time 0.10. Missing signals are excluded, never treated as zero. Each stored candidate records its weights version. Bins: at least 0.75 `high`, at least 0.55 `medium`, otherwise `low`. A match notification is sent only for a score of at least 0.65 ranked in the top 3. Weights and thresholds are tuned on the development set only (section 7).
229: 
230: ### 6.5 Candidates and retrieval
231: 
232: A candidate pair is a lost report and a found report where both are `open`, the reporters differ, the pair has not been dismissed, and the found time lies between 6 hours before the lost window starts and 30 days after it ends. Retrieval uses the HNSW index to fetch the nearest neighbours by text and by image, merges them with the location and time candidates, scores them all, and returns the top K (default 10). New reports trigger scoring in both directions, and each (lost, found, model version, weights version) is scored once. Ties break by the older found report, then by ID.
233: 
234: ### 6.6 Explanations
235: 
236: The contribution of a signal is `wᵢ sᵢ / Σ wⱼ` over the available signals, so contributions sum to the score. The explanation lists the signals contributing at least 10% of the score (or the top 3) in plain sentences, for example "Similar description", "Visually similar photo", "Reported in a nearby building", and "Found 3 hours after you reported it lost". It never includes private details.
237: 
238: ## 7. Evaluation Design
239: 
240: **Research question:** does combining image similarity, semantic text similarity, and campus location and time signals improve lost-item retrieval compared with keyword-based search?
241: 
242: ### 7.1 Benchmark
243: 
244: - **Items:** 300 true items across the 12 categories, each with a lost report and a found report, plus 100 **background** found reports with no lost report (unclaimed items). A fixed campus tree of about 40 leaf locations is used.
245: - **Synthetic text:** each side is generated by a seeded grammar from the item's attributes (category, colour, material or brand-like descriptor, distinguishing feature). The lost and found sides use **different** lexicons and phrasing (for example "flask" and "bottle", "navy" and "dark blue"), each side drops at least one attribute, and a character-level typo rate of 2% is applied. Because both sides come from templates, a separate **human-written subset** of at least 60 items (two people writing blind to each other's text) is built and reported separately.
246: - **Photos:** a **real-photo subset** of at least 60 items, each photographed twice by different people with different angles and backgrounds; the other items have no photo. Image-based systems are evaluated on this subset.
247: - **Time and location:** the found time follows the lost time by a log-normal delay (median about 6 hours); the found location equals the true location with probability 0.6, is one level off with 0.3, and is random with 0.1. These are assumptions, and the noise ablations of 7.6 test how much the conclusions depend on them.
248: - **Ground truth:** exactly one true found report per lost report.
249: - **Query and pool:** each lost report is a query, and the candidate pool is all found reports in its split (true items plus the background reports).
250: - **Split:** 30% development (90 items) and 70% test (210 items), stratified by category, by item.
251: 
252: ### 7.2 Systems compared
253: 
254: | System | Description |
255: | --- | --- |
256: | A: keyword | BM25 over title and description |
257: | B: text embedding | Text signal only |
258: | C: image | Image signal only, on reports with photos |
259: | D: hybrid | Hand-weighted hybrid of 6.4 |
260: | E: learned fusion | Logistic regression over the signals and their missing-value indicators, trained on the development set |
261: | Ablations | Hybrid with one signal removed in turn (7.6) |
262: 
263: ### 7.3 Metrics
264: 
265: With one correct answer per query: **Recall@K** (equal to hit rate), **MRR**, **nDCG@K**, and **Precision@K** (capped at 1/K, so reported with that caveat), at K = 1, 3, 5 and 10. **Latency** at the 50th and 95th percentile, at 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000 candidates (synthetic vectors for scale), for approximate and exact search. End-to-end outcomes (verified returns, time to recovery, false claims, unclaimed rate) are operational metrics shown by the dashboard; the benchmark cannot measure them.
266: 
267: ### 7.4 Statistics
268: 
269: Confidence intervals come from a **bootstrap over queries** (1,000 resamples, fixed seed). Differences between systems use a **paired bootstrap** on the same queries. A system is called better only if the 95% interval of the difference excludes 0.
270: 
271: ### 7.5 Protocol and leakage control
272: 
273: Weights and the learned model are chosen on the **development set only**. The chosen configuration is written to a file, hashed, and **frozen**; the test set is evaluated once from that file. The tuning code has no access path to test labels, and a test enforces this. Every run records model names and versions, weights, random seed, dataset hash, git commit and hardware.
274: 
275: ### 7.6 Ablations and robustness
276: 
277: Remove each signal in turn; set 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100% of photos to missing; apply location noise (one level off) and time noise (24 hours off) to 0, 25 and 50% of the found reports. Report each with confidence intervals.

145: ### 5.2 Time windows
146: 
147: A report gives a time and a precision. It becomes a **window** `[start, end]` in UTC: `exact` is a zero-length window, `day` is the local calendar day, and `morning`, `afternoon`, `evening` and `night` are the local periods 06:00 to 12:00, 12:00 to 17:00, 17:00 to 22:00 and 22:00 to 06:00 (initial, configurable). Local time uses the reporter's IANA timezone.

154: | `under_review` | `approved`, `rejected`, `needs_more_info` (moderator), `withdrawn` (claimant) |
155: | `needs_more_info` | `submitted` (claimant adds evidence), `withdrawn` (claimant) |
156: | `approved` | `completed` (system, on handover completion), `expired` (system, code expired), `withdrawn` (claimant; cancels the handover) |
157: | `rejected`, `completed`, `expired`, `withdrawn` | none |
158: 
159: A claim also has a flag `escalated` when it waits more than 14 days. A user has at most 3 active claims (those not in a final state) and at most one claim per found item. A moderator cannot decide a claim on an item they reported or a claim they made.
160: 
161: ### 5.4 Handover codes
162: 
163: - When a claim is approved, the system issues a code of **8 characters** from the alphabet `0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ` (40 bits), drawn from a cryptographically secure random source, and shows it **only to the claimant** (in-app and by email).
164: - Only an HMAC-SHA-256 of the code under a server secret is stored. Comparison is constant-time.
165: - Input is normalised by uppercasing, dropping spaces and hyphens, and mapping `O` to `0` and `I` or `L` to `1`.
166: - The code expires **48 hours** after issue (*initial*), works **once**, and locks the handover after **5 wrong attempts** (HTTP 423 until a moderator reissues it; at most 3 reissues). With 5 attempts against 2⁴⁰ possible codes, a random guess succeeds with probability about 4.5 × 10⁻¹².
167: - At the desk, the claimant shows the code and the moderator types it in. The moderator sees only success or failure, and must record an identity-check note to complete the handover.
168: - If the code expires, the claim becomes `expired` and the item returns to `open`.
169: 
170: ### 5.5 Retention and deletion
171: 
172: A daily job, driven by an injected clock in tests, expires found reports after 90 days, deletes closed reports' photos after 30 days and claim evidence after 30 days, and purges old audit rows through a separate privileged role. Account deletion removes personal data, anonymises reports and keeps audit rows under a pseudonymous ID.
173: 
174: ### 5.6 PII scanning of public text
175: 
176: Title and description are scanned before saving. Flagged kinds are: `card_number` (13 to 19 digits that pass the Luhn check), `long_number` (any run of 9 or more digits, ignoring spaces and hyphens), `phone` (a phone-number pattern) and `email`. A flagged public field is rejected with `pii_detected` (the kind, never the value). Private details may contain such text and show a warning only.
177: 
178: ### 5.7 Photo pipeline
179: 
180: Allowed types are JPEG, PNG and WebP, decided by file content (magic bytes), up to 5 MB and 6,000 × 6,000 pixels, with at most 3 photos per report. Each upload is decoded with a pixel-limit guard, stripped of all metadata (including GPS), re-encoded, resized to at most 1,600 pixels on the long side, thumbnailed, and stored under a random UUID key with a 64-bit difference hash. Images are served only through an authorised route. Found photos wait for moderator approval and are non-public in sensitive categories.
181: 
182: **Categories (fixed list, initial):** `bottle`, `bag`, `wallet`, `phone`, `laptop_tablet`, `earphones`, `keys`, `id_card`, `clothing`, `book`, `accessory`, `other`.
183: 
184: ## 6. Matching
185: 
186: ### 6.1 Models and embeddings
187: 
188: | Purpose | Starting choice (verify each licence before use) |
189: | --- | --- |
190: | Text embeddings | A small sentence-embedding model such as `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384 dimensions) |
191: | Image and cross-modal embeddings | A CLIP-family model such as ViT-B/32 (512 dimensions), giving image vectors and text vectors in one space |
192: | Stretch comparison | A SigLIP-family model, as the blueprint suggests |
193: 
194: - Weights are downloaded **at image build time** with pinned revisions and checksums and baked into the image, so the running system makes no outbound model calls (D4).
195: - Every embedding row stores `model_name`, `model_version` and `dimension`, and vectors are L2-normalised. Matching compares only vectors of the same version. Vectors live in PostgreSQL with the **pgvector** extension and an HNSW index using cosine distance.
196: - Embeddings are computed by background workers, never during a web request.
197: 
198: ### 6.2 Signals
199: 
200: Each signal is a number in [0, 1] or `null` when it cannot be computed.

170: * **What was built:**
171:   * **Pure Domain Scoring & Candidate Logic (`app/domain/matching.py`):**
172:     * Text score (AC-51): $\max(0, \text{cosine})$ of normalized embeddings (tested on cosine 0.82 $\to$ 0.82, -0.10 $\to$ 0.0).
173:     * Time score (AC-52): Overlapping windows score 1.0; asymmetric exponential decay if found after lost ($\exp(-\text{gap}/48)$; 12h $\to$ 0.7788, 48h $\to$ 0.3679) and if found before lost ($\exp(-\text{gap}/6)$; 6h $\to$ 0.3679, 12h $\to$ 0.1353).
174:     * Hybrid score with dynamic weight renormalization (AC-53, AC-54): Sums $\frac{\sum w_i s_i}{\sum w_i}$ strictly over non-null signals, never treating missing signals as zero (signals 0.8, 0.6, 0.7, 0.5 score 0.685; with image missing, weights renormalize over 0.65 yielding 0.7308; a text-only pair scores exactly its text score).
175:     * Image signal determination (AC-55): Image-to-image similarity when both have photos, text-to-image cross-similarity when exactly one has photos, and null when neither does.
176:     * Candidate constraints validation (AC-56): Both reports `open`, reporters differ, pair not dismissed, found item not reserved or returned, found time between 6 hours before lost window starts and 30 days after it ends.
177:     * Deterministic tie-breaking (AC-57): Sorts by `score DESC`, then `found.created_at ASC` (older found item first), then `found.id ASC`.
178:     * Explainability & Exact Additivity (AC-59): Signal contributions $c_i = \frac{w_i s_i}{\sum w_j}$ sum to the combined score within $10^{-9}$; plain language explanations for signals contributing $\ge 10\%$ of score (or top 3).
179:   * **Database Infrastructure & Migrations (`0007_match_candidates.py`, `0008_hnsw_indexes.py`):**
180:     * Tables `match_candidates` and `match_feedback` with unique constraint `(lost_id, found_id, weights_version)` and status indexes.
181:     * pgvector HNSW vector cosine indexes (`vector_cosine_ops`) created on `text_embeddings` and `image_embeddings` for approximate nearest-neighbor search.
182:   * **Matching Services & API (`services/matching.py`, `api/matches.py`):**
183:     * `compute_matches_for_report`: Bidirectional candidate scoring (lost triggers found, found triggers lost), idempotent upsert, and transactional match suggestion notification creation for top 3 candidates scoring $\ge 0.65$ (AC-63, AC-65).
184:     * `GET /api/reports/{id}/matches` (AC-58): Owner-only matching endpoint (404 anti-enumeration for foreign users) returning score, bin, signals, explanations, and strictly whitelisted public found item summaries (`PublicFoundItemSummary`).
185:     * Privacy Canary Contract (AC-60): Canary string in private details never appears in explanations, responses, notifications, or logs.
186:     * Permanent Dismissal (AC-61): `POST /api/matches/{id}/dismiss` marks candidate as dismissed, records feedback, and prevents dismissed pairs from reappearing.
187:     * AI Advisory Enforcement (AC-62): Verified that artificial score updates (e.g. 0.99) never alter report or claim status.
188:     * Model & Weights Versioning (AC-64): Stores `weights_version` and `model_versions`; changing weights preserves historical runs.
189:     * HNSW Recall & Latency Verification (AC-66, AC-67): Verified HNSW recall@10 $\ge 90\%$ against exact flat search and retrieval/scoring latency $< 200$ ms at p50 and $< 800$ ms at p95.
190: * **Why it is designed that way:**
191:   * **Dynamic Weight Renormalization:** Treating missing signals (such as an absent photo) as zero would severely penalize honest reporters who lost an item for which they had no picture. Renormalizing remaining weights preserves fairness across varying signal availability.
192:   * **Asymmetric Time Decay:** While an item cannot physically be found before it was lost (except for slight human reporting errors in timestamps, allowing a steep 6-hour half-decay), lost items commonly sit undetected in campus hallways or lost-and-found bins for days or weeks (represented by a gradual 48-hour decay).
193:   * **Layering & Separation of Concerns:** Domain matching calculations contain zero database or framework imports, allowing the exact formulas and worked numbers from the specification to be tested with high-speed, deterministic unit tests.
194:   * **AI as Advisory Only:** Under campus policy and ethical guidelines, automated similarity scores serve exclusively to surface candidate suggestions to human owners and staff, never triggering automated lifecycle or claim decisions.
195: * **One thing that could go wrong:**
196:   * **HNSW Index Autogenerate Drift:** Creating pgvector HNSW indexes in raw SQL without declaring them in SQLAlchemy model `__table_args__` causes `alembic check` to flag unmanaged indexes as dropped. Explicitly declaring `Index("ix_text_embeddings_hnsw", "vector", postgresql_using="hnsw", postgresql_ops={"vector": "vector_cosine_ops"})` in the model metadata keeps database state and Python schema in lockstep.
197: * **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
198:   1. *Why must missing multimodal signals be dynamically excluded and weights renormalized rather than imputed as 0.0 in lost-and-found matching?*
199:   2. *What is the mathematical justification for an asymmetric exponential decay function in the time similarity score?*
200:   3. *How does the explanation generator guarantee that the sum of individual signal contributions strictly equals the combined hybrid score?*

+### Step 8: Claims and Moderation (AC-75 to AC-85)
+* **What was built:**
+  * **Pure Domain Logic (`app/domain/claims.py`):**
+    * Exhaustive lifecycle transitions (AC-76): `submitted` $\to$ `under_review`, `withdrawn`; `under_review` $\to$ `approved`, `rejected`, `needs_more_info`, `withdrawn`; `needs_more_info` $\to$ `submitted`, `withdrawn`; `approved` $\to$ `completed`, `expired`, `withdrawn`; terminal states `rejected`, `completed`, `expired`, `withdrawn`.
+    * Validation & Prompt Answers (AC-75): Evidence text strictly 20 to 2000 characters; answers to every verification prompt; anti-self-claim; prevention of duplicate claims on the same found item.
+    * Abuse Prevention & Active Claim Limits (AC-84): Normal limit of 3 active claims; users with 3 rejected claims within 30 days are automatically limited to 1 active claim and flagged as `claimant_flagged=True` for staff.
+    * Concurrency & Review Locks (AC-78): Opening a claim assigns an exclusive 30-minute lock (`lock_expires_at = now + 30m`, `locked_by_id = mod.id`); prevents concurrent moderator decisions with HTTP 409 `claim_locked`; expired locks automatically become available to other staff.
+    * Conflict of Interest (AC-80): A moderator cannot decide a claim on an item they reported, or a claim they filed themselves (HTTP 403 `conflict_of_interest`).
+    * Escalation (AC-85): Unreviewed claims older than 14 days are marked `escalated=True` and prioritized first in the queue.
+  * **Database Infrastructure & Migrations (`0009_claims_table.py`):**
+    * Table `claims` with foreign keys to `item_reports` (found and optional lost) and `users` (claimant, reviewer, locked_by), JSONB answers and image_ids, timestamps, and composite performance indexes (`(claimant_id, status)`, `(found_id, status)`, `(status, submitted_at)`).
+  * **Services & API Endpoints (`services/claims.py`, `api/claims.py`, `api/moderation.py`):**
+    * `POST /api/claims`: Secure claim creation with CSRF, prompt validation, and active-claim limits.
+    * `GET /api/claims/{id}`: Privacy-enforced claim detail (AC-77); visible strictly to claimant and moderators (404 anti-enumeration for finder and other users).
+    * `POST /api/claims/{id}/withdraw` (AC-83): Claimant withdrawal; withdrawing an approved claim cancels the handover and reverts the found item back to `open`.
+    * `PATCH /api/claims/{id}/evidence` (AC-82): Allows claimants to amend evidence when in `needs_more_info`, transitioning back to `submitted` and re-entering the queue.
+    * `GET /api/mod/queue` (AC-78, AC-85): Unified moderator queue displaying pending reports, duplicate images, and active claims, ordered with escalated claims first, then submission time ascending.
+    * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/open`: Moderator lock acquisition for 30 minutes.
+    * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/approve` (AC-79, AC-81): Decision note $\ge 10$ characters, reserves found item (`item_reports.status = "reserved"`), blocks conflicting approvals (HTTP 409 `item_already_reserved`), creates transactional notification, and logs `claim.approved`.
+    * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/reject` (AC-79): Decision note $\ge 10$ characters, marks claim `rejected`, logs `claim.rejected`, and notifies claimant.
+    * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/request-info`: Decision note $\ge 10$ characters, transitions claim to `needs_more_info`, releases review lock, and notifies claimant.
+* **Why it is designed that way:**
+  * **Default-Deny Claim Privacy:** Claimants submit sensitive evidence (e.g., distinguishing engravings, unique scratches, purchase receipts, answers to private verification prompts). If this evidence were visible to the item finder or other campus users, malicious actors could copy those details and file fraudulent counter-claims.
+  * **Time-Bound Exclusive Review Locks:** In campus facilities with multiple staff members on duty, concurrent reviews without locking cause race conditions where two moderators approve competing claims simultaneously or issue duplicate handover instructions. The 30-minute lock prevents collision while an automatic expiration ensures that an abandoned review session does not lock a student's claim indefinitely.
+  * **Strict Conflict-of-Interest Controls:** Academic integrity and asset security require that staff members cannot self-certify ownership of items they reported finding or approve items they claim to have lost.
+  * **Reversible Reservation on Withdrawal:** When a claimant withdraws after approval (for example, if they locate their misplaced item at home), the found report is automatically returned to `open` so other students or queued claims can be evaluated without manual administrator intervention.
+* **One thing that could go wrong:**
+  * **Orphaned Locks on Abandoned Sessions:** If a moderator opens a claim and closes their tab or browser without making a decision, the claim remains locked until the 30-minute window expires. Handled by checking `lock_expires_at > now` in real time: once expired, any authorized moderator can re-open and acquire the review lock without manual unlock actions.
+* **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
+  1. *Why must the finder of a found item be prevented from seeing claim evidence and prompt answers submitted by claimants?*
+  2. *How does the system enforce concurrency control and prevent duplicate decisions when multiple moderators review claims simultaneously?*
+  3. *What happens to a found report's status and subsequent claims if an approved claimant withdraws their claim prior to handover?*

190: * **Why it is designed that way:**
191:   * **Dynamic Weight Renormalization:** Treating missing signals (such as an absent photo) as zero would severely penalize honest reporters who lost an item for which they had no picture. Renormalizing remaining weights preserves fairness across varying signal availability.
192:   * **Asymmetric Time Decay:** While an item cannot physically be found before it was lost (except for slight human reporting errors in timestamps, allowing a steep 6-hour half-decay), lost items commonly sit undetected in campus hallways or lost-and-found bins for days or weeks (represented by a gradual 48-hour decay).
193:   * **Layering & Separation of Concerns:** Domain matching calculations contain zero database or framework imports, allowing the exact formulas and worked numbers from the specification to be tested with high-speed, deterministic unit tests.
194:   * **AI as Advisory Only:** Under campus policy and ethical guidelines, automated similarity scores serve exclusively to surface candidate suggestions to human owners and staff, never triggering automated lifecycle or claim decisions.
195: * **One thing that could go wrong:**
196:   * **HNSW Index Autogenerate Drift:** Creating pgvector HNSW indexes in raw SQL without declaring them in SQLAlchemy model `__table_args__` causes `alembic check` to flag unmanaged indexes as dropped. Explicitly declaring `Index("ix_text_embeddings_hnsw", "vector", postgresql_using="hnsw", postgresql_ops={"vector": "vector_cosine_ops"})` in the model metadata keeps database state and Python schema in lockstep.

11: ### Step 8: Claims and Moderation (AC-75 to AC-85)
12: * **What was built:**
13:   * **Pure Domain Logic (`app/domain/claims.py`):**
14:     * Exhaustive lifecycle transitions (AC-76): `submitted` $\to$ `under_review`, `withdrawn`; `under_review` $\to$ `approved`, `rejected`, `needs_more_info`, `withdrawn`; `needs_more_info` $\to$ `submitted`, `withdrawn`; `approved` $\to$ `completed`, `expired`, `withdrawn`; terminal states `rejected`, `completed`, `expired`, `withdrawn`.
15:     * Validation & Prompt Answers (AC-75): Evidence text strictly 20 to 2000 characters; answers to every verification prompt; anti-self-claim; prevention of duplicate claims on the same found item.
16:     * Abuse Prevention & Active Claim Limits (AC-84): Normal limit of 3 active claims; users with 3 rejected claims within 30 days are automatically limited to 1 active claim and flagged as `claimant_flagged=True` for staff.
17:     * Concurrency & Review Locks (AC-78): Opening a claim assigns an exclusive 30-minute lock (`lock_expires_at = now + 30m`, `locked_by_id = mod.id`); prevents concurrent moderator decisions with HTTP 409 `claim_locked`; expired locks automatically become available to other staff.
18:     * Conflict of Interest (AC-80): A moderator cannot decide a claim on an item they reported, or a claim they filed themselves (HTTP 403 `conflict_of_interest`).
19:     * Escalation (AC-85): Unreviewed claims older than 14 days are marked `escalated=True` and prioritized first in the queue.
20:   * **Database Infrastructure & Migrations (`0009_claims_table.py`):**
21:     * Table `claims` with foreign keys to `item_reports` (found and optional lost) and `users` (claimant, reviewer, locked_by), JSONB answers and image_ids, timestamps, and composite performance indexes (`(claimant_id, status)`, `(found_id, status)`, `(status, submitted_at)`).
22:   * **Services & API Endpoints (`services/claims.py`, `api/claims.py`, `api/moderation.py`):**
23:     * `POST /api/claims`: Secure claim creation with CSRF, prompt validation, and active-claim limits.
24:     * `GET /api/claims/{id}`: Privacy-enforced claim detail (AC-77); visible strictly to claimant and moderators (404 anti-enumeration for finder and other users).
25:     * `POST /api/claims/{id}/withdraw` (AC-83): Claimant withdrawal; withdrawing an approved claim cancels the handover and reverts the found item back to `open`.
26:     * `PATCH /api/claims/{id}/evidence` (AC-82): Allows claimants to amend evidence when in `needs_more_info`, transitioning back to `submitted` and re-entering the queue.
27:     * `GET /api/mod/queue` (AC-78, AC-85): Unified moderator queue displaying pending reports, duplicate images, and active claims, ordered with escalated claims first, then submission time ascending.
28:     * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/open`: Moderator lock acquisition for 30 minutes.
29:     * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/approve` (AC-79, AC-81): Decision note $\ge 10$ characters, reserves found item (`item_reports.status = "reserved"`), blocks conflicting approvals (HTTP 409 `item_already_reserved`), creates transactional notification, and logs `claim.approved`.
30:     * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/reject` (AC-79): Decision note $\ge 10$ characters, marks claim `rejected`, logs `claim.rejected`, and notifies claimant.
31:     * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/request-info`: Decision note $\ge 10$ characters, transitions claim to `needs_more_info`, releases review lock, and notifies claimant.
32: * **Why it is designed that way:**
33:   * **Default-Deny Claim Privacy:** Claimants submit sensitive evidence (e.g., distinguishing engravings, unique scratches, purchase receipts, answers to private verification prompts). If this evidence were visible to the item finder or other campus users, malicious actors could copy those details and file fraudulent counter-claims.
34:   * **Time-Bound Exclusive Review Locks:** In campus facilities with multiple staff members on duty, concurrent reviews without locking cause race conditions where two moderators approve competing claims simultaneously or issue duplicate handover instructions. The 30-minute lock prevents collision while an automatic expiration ensures that an abandoned review session does not lock a student's claim indefinitely.
35:   * **Strict Conflict-of-Interest Controls:** Academic integrity and asset security require that staff members cannot self-certify ownership of items they reported finding or approve items they claim to have lost.
36:   * **Reversible Reservation on Withdrawal:** When a claimant withdraws after approval (for example, if they locate their misplaced item at home), the found report is automatically returned to `open` so other students or queued claims can be evaluated without manual administrator intervention.
37: * **One thing that could go wrong:**
38:   * **Orphaned Locks on Abandoned Sessions:** If a moderator opens a claim and closes their tab or browser without making a decision, the claim remains locked until the 30-minute window expires. Handled by checking `lock_expires_at > now` in real time: once expired, any authorized moderator can re-open and acquire the review lock without manual unlock actions.

223: * **Why it is designed that way:**
224:   * **Default-Deny Claim Privacy:** Claimants submit sensitive evidence (e.g., distinguishing engravings, unique scratches, purchase receipts, answers to private verification prompts). If this evidence were visible to the item finder or other campus users, malicious actors could copy those details and file fraudulent counter-claims.
225:   * **Time-Bound Exclusive Review Locks:** In campus facilities with multiple staff members on duty, concurrent reviews without locking cause race conditions where two moderators approve competing claims simultaneously or issue duplicate handover instructions. The 30-minute lock prevents collision while an automatic expiration ensures that an abandoned review session does not lock a student's claim indefinitely.
226:   * **Strict Conflict-of-Interest Controls:** Academic integrity and asset security require that staff members cannot self-certify ownership of items they reported finding or approve items they claim to have lost.
227:   * **Reversible Reservation on Withdrawal:** When a claimant withdraws after approval (for example, if they locate their misplaced item at home), the found report is automatically returned to `open` so other students or queued claims can be evaluated without manual administrator intervention.
228: * **One thing that could go wrong:**
229:   * **Orphaned Locks on Abandoned Sessions:** If a moderator opens a claim and closes their tab or browser without making a decision, the claim remains locked until the 30-minute window expires. Handled by checking `lock_expires_at > now` in real time: once expired, any authorized moderator can re-open and acquire the review lock without manual unlock actions.

+### Step 9: Handover Codes and Completion (AC-86 to AC-96)
+* **What was built:**
+  * **Pure Domain Logic (`app/domain/handover.py`):**
+    * Human-friendly Base32 alphabet `0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ` (32 characters, excluding ambiguous glyphs `I`, `L`, `O`), generating 8-character codes with $\log_2(32^8) = 40$ bits of entropy (AC-86).
+    * Normalization routine (AC-88): strips whitespace and hyphens, converts to uppercase, and maps optical confusions (`O` $\to$ `0`, `I` $\to$ `1`, `L` $\to$ `1`).
+    * Cryptographic security (AC-87, AC-95): stores strictly secret-keyed HMAC-SHA-256 digests (`code_hmac`), never plaintext; verification performs constant-time comparison via `hmac.compare_digest` over HMAC digests.
+    * Injected-clock expiration (AC-89): 48-hour valid lifetime from issuance.
+    * Rate limiting and lockout bounds (AC-91): maximum 5 failed attempts per code; 6th attempt locks the handover and returns HTTP 423 `handover_locked`.
+    * Reissue bounds (AC-92): allows up to 3 reissues per claim; each reissue resets failed attempt counter and restarts the 48-hour expiration clock.
+  * **Database Infrastructure & Migrations (`0010_handover_table.py`):**
+    * `handovers` table with foreign key to `claims.id`, `code_hmac` string(64), attempts, max_attempts, reissue_count, max_reissues, status, `issued_at`, `expires_at`, `verified_at`, `verified_by_id`, and `identity_note`.
+    * Unique constraint `uq_handovers_claim_id` ensuring 1-to-1 relationship between approved claims and handover codes.
+  * **Services & Handover Desk API Endpoints (`services/handover.py`, `api/handover.py`):**
+    * `issue_handover`: invoked automatically upon claim approval (AC-79), generating code and dispatching transactional in-app/email notification to claimant.
+    * `GET /api/mod/handovers/{claim_id}` (AC-96): desk status view showing status, attempts left, and lock state, strictly excluding plaintext code and HMAC.
+    * `POST /api/mod/handovers/{claim_id}/verify` (AC-90, AC-91, AC-93): verifies code and records identity check note ($\ge 10$ characters); duplicate verification of verified code returns HTTP 409 `code_used`.
+    * `POST /api/mod/handovers/{claim_id}/reissue` (AC-92): moderator reissue with reason ($\ge 10$ characters); blocks 4th reissue with HTTP 409 `reissue_limit_exceeded`.
+    * `POST /api/mod/handovers/expire` (AC-94): sweep operation that transitions expired handovers and approved claims to `expired` and returns reserved items to `open`.
+    * Single atomic completion transaction (AC-93): transitions claim to `completed`, found report to `returned`, linked lost report to `resolved`, bulk-rejects competing open claims on the same found item with reason `item_returned`, writes immutable audit log, and notifies claimant and finder.
+    * Privacy-preserving claimant delivery (AC-96): claimant views single-use handover code in `GET /api/claims/{id}`; moderators and third parties never receive code or HMAC.
+* **Why it is designed that way:**
+  * **Zero-Knowledge Handover Secrets:** Neither database administrators reviewing production tables nor desk staff examining claimant records can view plaintext handover codes. Because only the claimant receives the raw code, fraud by staff impersonating claimants is structurally eliminated.
+  * **Optical Normalization for Human Reliability:** Lost-and-found transactions occur in physical campus offices where students transcribe codes from mobile screens or handwriting. Normalizing `O` $\to$ `0` and `I/L` $\to$ `1` prevents accidental lockouts without compromising security.
+  * **All-or-Nothing Atomic Completion:** If marking the item returned succeeded but rejecting competing claims failed halfway, multiple students would continue waiting for review of an item already handed over. Encapsulating claim completion, inventory updates, competing claim rejections, notifications, and audit logs into a single ACID transaction guarantees system consistency.
+* **One thing that could go wrong:**
+  * **Timing Attacks on Code Verification:** Standard string comparison (`==`) exits early upon encountering the first non-matching character, allowing an attacker with precise network measurements to guess characters incrementally. Mitigated by hashing candidate input with secret-keyed HMAC-SHA-256 and comparing digests using `hmac.compare_digest`.
+* **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
+  1. *Why does the handover verification system store HMAC-SHA-256 digests rather than raw handover codes or simple SHA-256 hashes?*
+  2. *How does the system ensure that a student typing a handwritten or mistyped code (e.g., using letter 'O' instead of digit '0') is not penalized with a failed attempt?*
+  3. *What specific state transitions occur across claims, lost reports, and found reports within the atomic completion transaction when a handover is verified?*

1: # SPEC.md: Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network
2: 
3: **Version:** 1.0 (draft, based on *Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network: Project Blueprint*)
4: **Last updated:** 2026-10-18
5: **Methodology:** Spec-Driven Development. Every requirement has an ID, and every acceptance criterion (AC) becomes at least one automated test or one recorded measurement.
6: 
7: > Numbers marked *initial* (thresholds, weights, targets) are starting values. If you change one after measuring, record the change in the Decisions Log (section 20). The results of the evaluation are **findings**, not targets: report whichever way they fall.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## 1. Overview
12: 
13: A full-stack web application where campus users report lost and found belongings, the system suggests likely matches using text, photos, campus location and time, and campus staff verify claims and complete handovers with a one-time code. AI suggestions are **advice for humans**: no score ever approves a claim or changes a status.
14: 
15: The project has two halves of equal weight. The **product** half is a trustworthy workflow: privacy-aware public listings, evidence-based claims, moderator review, expiring single-use handover codes, an audit trail, and retention rules. The **research** half asks a measurable question: *does combining text, image, location and time signals retrieve lost items better than keyword search?* It is answered on a controlled benchmark with proper splits, confidence intervals and ablations.
16: 
17: The blueprint itself notes that AI-assisted lost-and-found systems already exist. This project does not claim a novel idea. Its contribution is a careful, secure, explainable campus workflow and an honestly measured comparison.
18: 
19: ### Aim
20: 
21: Build a secure, campus-aware lost-and-found platform with explainable multimodal matching, a verified claim and handover process, and a reproducible evaluation of hybrid retrieval against keyword and single-signal baselines, deployed as a service you can open in a browser on your computer or local network.
22: 
23: ### Inputs
24: 
25: | Input | Details |
26: | --- | --- |
27: | Accounts | Campus email, password, display name (optional) |
28: | Reports | Lost or found: title, description, category, time (with precision), campus location (any level), up to 3 photos, optional private details and verification prompts (found reports) |
29: | Claims | Evidence text, answers to verification prompts, up to 3 private evidence photos |
30: | Moderator actions | Approve or remove reports, decide claims, issue and verify handover codes |
31: | Campus data | A location tree and building adjacency, maintained by admins |
32: | Models | A pinned text-embedding model and a pinned image-text model (section 6.1) |
33: | Benchmark data | A synthetic generator plus a small real-photo subset, with a data card (section 7) |
34: | Configuration | Environment variables: database URL, secrets, allowed email domains, SMTP, retention periods, model versions |
35: 
36: ### Outputs
37: 
38: | Output | Details |
39: | --- | --- |
40: | Searchable listings | Found items visible to authenticated campus users, without private details |
41: | Ranked match suggestions | Top candidates for each report, with a score, a bin and a plain-language explanation |
42: | Claims and handovers | Reviewed claims, expiring handover codes, completed returns with an audit trail |
43: | Notifications | In-app and email, with no private details |
44: | Analytics | Recovery rate, time to recovery, unclaimed rate, volume and queue age |
45: | Evaluation results | Tables and plots of retrieval quality, ablations and latency, with confidence intervals and recorded model versions |
46: | Deployed service | The web application, running in containers at `http://localhost:8080` (and over HTTPS on the local network) |
47: 
48: ### Requirements at a glance
49: 
50: - **Functional:** FR-01 to FR-20 (section 14).
51: - **Privacy, safety and trust:** P1 to P7 and S1 to S4 (section 4).
52: - **Security:** SEC1 to SEC12 (section 12). **Deployment:** D1 to D10 (section 13).
53: - **Non-functional:** section 17.
54: - **Acceptance criteria:** AC-01 to AC-149 (section 15), mapped to the blueprint in section 16.
55: 
56: ## 2. Goals, Scope and Non-Goals
57: 
58: **Goals**
59: 1. Accounts with roles (user, moderator, admin) and campus-email verification.
60: 2. A hierarchical campus location model that tolerates approximate locations.
61: 3. Lost and found reports with a safe photo pipeline and a defined lifecycle.
62: 4. Searchable listings that never expose private details.
63: 5. Background embedding jobs and a hybrid matching engine with explanations.
64: 6. Notifications (in-app and email) through a reliable outbox.
65: 7. Claims, moderator review, and one-time handover codes.
66: 8. An append-only audit log, retention rules, and data export and deletion.
67: 9. An analytics dashboard.
68: 10. A reproducible evaluation of keyword, text, image and hybrid retrieval.
69: 11. A tested, documented, deployed system.
70: 
71: **Non-goals (v1)**
72: - Campus single sign-on, mobile apps, push notifications, or SMS.
73: - Automatic ownership decisions, or any AI action without human review.
74: - GPS tracking or precise indoor positioning.
75: - Facial recognition. Photos are never used to identify people.
76: - Evidence that the system improves real-world recovery rates (only a pilot could show that; the benchmark does not).
77: 
78: **Stretch** (only after every required criterion passes): a SigLIP-family model comparison, multilingual text, face and number-plate blurring in photos, learning from dismissals, campus SSO, and a digest email.
79: 
80: ## 3. Roles and Access Control
81: 
82: | Role | Who | Can |
83: | --- | --- | --- |
84: | `user` | A verified campus account | Report items, browse found items, see matches for their own lost reports, claim found items, manage their own data |
85: | `moderator` | Authorised campus staff | Everything a user can, plus review reports and images, decide claims, issue and verify handover codes, see private details and the dashboard |
86: | `admin` | A small number of administrators | Everything a moderator can, plus manage locations, roles, jobs, the audit log and the evaluation page |
87: 
88: | Capability | Anonymous | User | Moderator | Admin |
89: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
90: | Register, verify email, log in | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
91: | Browse found items (public view) | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
92: | Create lost or found reports | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
93: | See own reports and matches | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
94: | See other users' lost reports | No | No | Yes | Yes |
95: | See private details and exact location of a found report | No | Reporter only | Yes | Yes |
96: | Approve or remove reports and images | No | No | Yes | Yes |
97: | Submit a claim (not on their own found item) | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
98: | See claim evidence | No | Claimant only | Yes | Yes |
99: | Decide claims (subject to the conflict rule) | No | No | Yes | Yes |
100: | Issue, reissue and verify handover codes | No | No | Yes | Yes |

105: ## 4. Privacy, Safety and Trust Rules
106: 
107: | ID | Rule |
108: | --- | --- |
109: | **P1 Default-deny public views** | Every response a normal user receives is built from an explicit whitelist of fields. Private details, verification prompts, reporter identity, exact locations, private images, claim evidence, handover codes and hashes never appear in a public view, an explanation, a notification or a log. |
110: | **P2 Private claim evidence** | Evidence and answers are visible only to the claimant and moderators, never to the finder. |
111: | **P3 Data minimisation** | Collect only an email address and an optional display name. No phone number, no student ID, no precise location. |
112: | **P4 Retention** | Found items expire after 90 days unclaimed; photos are deleted 30 days after closure; claim evidence 30 days after the claim closes; audit rows after 365 days (all *initial* and configurable). |
113: | **P5 Anti-scraping** | A login is required to browse, IDs are unguessable, browsing is rate-limited, and new accounts need a verified campus email. |
114: | **P6 Abuse controls** | Per-user claim limits, a flag for repeated rejected claims, and a conflict-of-interest rule for moderators. |
115: | **P7 Evaluation data** | Benchmark data contains no faces or personal data, with consent and licences recorded and a data card. Real users' reports are never used for evaluation. |
116: | **S1 AI is advisory** | Scores and explanations are suggestions. No code path changes a report, claim or handover state because of a score. |
117: | **S2 Human gates** | Found items are published after moderator review (default), claims are decided by a moderator, and handovers are completed by a moderator. |
118: | **S3 Transparent explanations** | Each suggestion shows which signals contributed and how much, in plain language. |
119: | **S4 Sensitive categories** | Items in the categories `id_card` and `wallet` never show photos publicly, and staff handle their details as private. |
120: 
121: ## 5. Domain Rules
122: 
123: ### 5.1 Report lifecycle
124: 
125: **Found report**
126: 
127: | State | Meaning | Legal next states (by whom) |
128: | --- | --- | --- |
129: | `pending_review` | Awaiting moderator approval | `open` (moderator approves), `removed` (moderator) |
130: | `open` | Listed and matchable | `reserved` (system, when a claim is approved), `closed` (reporter or moderator), `removed` (moderator), `unclaimed_expired` (system after the retention period) |
131: | `reserved` | A claim is approved and a handover is pending | `returned` (system, on handover completion), `open` (system, if the handover is cancelled or expires) |
132: | `returned` | Handed over | none |
133: | `unclaimed_expired` | Not claimed in time; a disposition is recorded | none |
134: | `closed`, `removed` | Ended by the reporter or a moderator | none |
135: 
136: **Lost report**
137: 
138: | State | Legal next states (by whom) |
139: | --- | --- |
140: | `open` | `resolved` (system on a completed handover, or the reporter), `closed` (reporter), `removed` (moderator), `expired` (system) |
141: | `resolved`, `closed`, `removed`, `expired` | none |
142: 
143: Every other transition returns 409 `invalid_transition`. A `reserved` item is excluded from matching and from new claims (409 `item_reserved`).
144: 
145: ### 5.2 Time windows
146: 
147: A report gives a time and a precision. It becomes a **window** `[start, end]` in UTC: `exact` is a zero-length window, `day` is the local calendar day, and `morning`, `afternoon`, `evening` and `night` are the local periods 06:00 to 12:00, 12:00 to 17:00, 17:00 to 22:00 and 22:00 to 06:00 (initial, configurable). Local time uses the reporter's IANA timezone.
148: 
149: ### 5.3 Claim lifecycle
150: 
151: | State | Legal next states (by whom) |
152: | --- | --- |
153: | `submitted` | `under_review` (moderator opens it and takes the lock), `withdrawn` (claimant) |
154: | `under_review` | `approved`, `rejected`, `needs_more_info` (moderator), `withdrawn` (claimant) |
155: | `needs_more_info` | `submitted` (claimant adds evidence), `withdrawn` (claimant) |
156: | `approved` | `completed` (system, on handover completion), `expired` (system, code expired), `withdrawn` (claimant; cancels the handover) |
157: | `rejected`, `completed`, `expired`, `withdrawn` | none |
158: 
159: A claim also has a flag `escalated` when it waits more than 14 days. A user has at most 3 active claims (those not in a final state) and at most one claim per found item. A moderator cannot decide a claim on an item they reported or a claim they made.
160: 
161: ### 5.4 Handover codes
162: 
163: - When a claim is approved, the system issues a code of **8 characters** from the alphabet `0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ` (40 bits), drawn from a cryptographically secure random source, and shows it **only to the claimant** (in-app and by email).
164: - Only an HMAC-SHA-256 of the code under a server secret is stored. Comparison is constant-time.
165: - Input is normalised by uppercasing, dropping spaces and hyphens, and mapping `O` to `0` and `I` or `L` to `1`.
166: - The code expires **48 hours** after issue (*initial*), works **once**, and locks the handover after **5 wrong attempts** (HTTP 423 until a moderator reissues it; at most 3 reissues). With 5 attempts against 2⁴⁰ possible codes, a random guess succeeds with probability about 4.5 × 10⁻¹².
167: - At the desk, the claimant shows the code and the moderator types it in. The moderator sees only success or failure, and must record an identity-check note to complete the handover.
168: - If the code expires, the claim becomes `expired` and the item returns to `open`.
169: 
170: ### 5.5 Retention and deletion
171: 
172: A daily job, driven by an injected clock in tests, expires found reports after 90 days, deletes closed reports' photos after 30 days and claim evidence after 30 days, and purges old audit rows through a separate privileged role. Account deletion removes personal data, anonymises reports and keeps audit rows under a pseudonymous ID.
173: 
174: ### 5.6 PII scanning of public text
175: 
176: Title and description are scanned before saving. Flagged kinds are: `card_number` (13 to 19 digits that pass the Luhn check), `long_number` (any run of 9 or more digits, ignoring spaces and hyphens), `phone` (a phone-number pattern) and `email`. A flagged public field is rejected with `pii_detected` (the kind, never the value). Private details may contain such text and show a warning only.
177: 
178: ### 5.7 Photo pipeline
179: 
180: Allowed types are JPEG, PNG and WebP, decided by file content (magic bytes), up to 5 MB and 6,000 × 6,000 pixels, with at most 3 photos per report. Each upload is decoded with a pixel-limit guard, stripped of all metadata (including GPS), re-encoded, resized to at most 1,600 pixels on the long side, thumbnailed, and stored under a random UUID key with a 64-bit difference hash. Images are served only through an authorised route. Found photos wait for moderator approval and are non-public in sensitive categories.
181: 
182: **Categories (fixed list, initial):** `bottle`, `bag`, `wallet`, `phone`, `laptop_tablet`, `earphones`, `keys`, `id_card`, `clothing`, `book`, `accessory`, `other`.
183: 
184: ## 6. Matching
185: 
186: ### 6.1 Models and embeddings
187: 
188: | Purpose | Starting choice (verify each licence before use) |
189: | --- | --- |
190: | Text embeddings | A small sentence-embedding model such as `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384 dimensions) |
191: | Image and cross-modal embeddings | A CLIP-family model such as ViT-B/32 (512 dimensions), giving image vectors and text vectors in one space |
192: | Stretch comparison | A SigLIP-family model, as the blueprint suggests |
193: 
194: - Weights are downloaded **at image build time** with pinned revisions and checksums and baked into the image, so the running system makes no outbound model calls (D4).
195: - Every embedding row stores `model_name`, `model_version` and `dimension`, and vectors are L2-normalised. Matching compares only vectors of the same version. Vectors live in PostgreSQL with the **pgvector** extension and an HNSW index using cosine distance.
196: - Embeddings are computed by background workers, never during a web request.
197: 
198: ### 6.2 Signals
199: 
200: Each signal is a number in [0, 1] or `null` when it cannot be computed.
201: 
202: | Signal | Definition |
203: | --- | --- |
204: | Text | `max(0, cosine)` between the text embeddings of `category + title + description` |
205: | Image | Image-to-image `max(0, cosine)` when both reports have photos (the best pair of photos); otherwise text-to-image `max(0, cosine)` (a report's text against the other report's photo) when exactly one has photos; otherwise `null` |
206: | Location | The table in 6.3 |
207: | Time | The decay function in 6.3 |
208: 
209: ### 6.3 Location and time scores
210: 
211: **Location score** by the relationship between the two locations in the tree:
212: 
213: | Relationship | Score |
214: | --- | --- |
215: | Identical | 1.0 |
216: | One is an ancestor of the other | 0.8 |
217: | Share a floor or an area (lowest common ancestor is a floor or an area) | 0.7 |
218: | Share a building only | 0.6 |
219: | Different buildings that are adjacent | 0.5 |
220: | Same campus, not adjacent | 0.2 |
221: | Different campuses | 0.0 |
222: | A location is missing | `null` |
223: 
224: **Time score** compares the two windows. If they overlap, the score is 1. Otherwise let `gap` be the hours between them: if the found window is after the lost window, `score = exp(−gap / 48)`; if it is before, `score = exp(−gap / 6)`. The asymmetry reflects that a finder cannot find something before it was lost, apart from imprecise reporting.
225: 
226: ### 6.4 Hybrid score
227: 
228: `score = Σ wᵢ sᵢ / Σ wᵢ`, summed **only over signals that are not `null`**. Initial weights: text 0.40, image 0.35, location 0.15, time 0.10. Missing signals are excluded, never treated as zero. Each stored candidate records its weights version. Bins: at least 0.75 `high`, at least 0.55 `medium`, otherwise `low`. A match notification is sent only for a score of at least 0.65 ranked in the top 3. Weights and thresholds are tuned on the development set only (section 7).
229: 
230: ### 6.5 Candidates and retrieval
231: 
232: A candidate pair is a lost report and a found report where both are `open`, the reporters differ, the pair has not been dismissed, and the found time lies between 6 hours before the lost window starts and 30 days after it ends. Retrieval uses the HNSW index to fetch the nearest neighbours by text and by image, merges them with the location and time candidates, scores them all, and returns the top K (default 10). New reports trigger scoring in both directions, and each (lost, found, model version, weights version) is scored once. Ties break by the older found report, then by ID.
233: 
234: ### 6.6 Explanations
235: 
236: The contribution of a signal is `wᵢ sᵢ / Σ wⱼ` over the available signals, so contributions sum to the score. The explanation lists the signals contributing at least 10% of the score (or the top 3) in plain sentences, for example "Similar description", "Visually similar photo", "Reported in a nearby building", and "Found 3 hours after you reported it lost". It never includes private details.
237: 
238: ## 7. Evaluation Design
239: 
240: **Research question:** does combining image similarity, semantic text similarity, and campus location and time signals improve lost-item retrieval compared with keyword-based search?
241: 
242: ### 7.1 Benchmark
243: 
244: - **Items:** 300 true items across the 12 categories, each with a lost report and a found report, plus 100 **background** found reports with no lost report (unclaimed items). A fixed campus tree of about 40 leaf locations is used.
245: - **Synthetic text:** each side is generated by a seeded grammar from the item's attributes (category, colour, material or brand-like descriptor, distinguishing feature). The lost and found sides use **different** lexicons and phrasing (for example "flask" and "bottle", "navy" and "dark blue"), each side drops at least one attribute, and a character-level typo rate of 2% is applied. Because both sides come from templates, a separate **human-written subset** of at least 60 items (two people writing blind to each other's text) is built and reported separately.
246: - **Photos:** a **real-photo subset** of at least 60 items, each photographed twice by different people with different angles and backgrounds; the other items have no photo. Image-based systems are evaluated on this subset.
247: - **Time and location:** the found time follows the lost time by a log-normal delay (median about 6 hours); the found location equals the true location with probability 0.6, is one level off with 0.3, and is random with 0.1. These are assumptions, and the noise ablations of 7.6 test how much the conclusions depend on them.
248: - **Ground truth:** exactly one true found report per lost report.
249: - **Query and pool:** each lost report is a query, and the candidate pool is all found reports in its split (true items plus the background reports).
250: - **Split:** 30% development (90 items) and 70% test (210 items), stratified by category, by item.
251: 
252: ### 7.2 Systems compared
253: 
254: | System | Description |
255: | --- | --- |
256: | A: keyword | BM25 over title and description |
257: | B: text embedding | Text signal only |
258: | C: image | Image signal only, on reports with photos |
259: | D: hybrid | Hand-weighted hybrid of 6.4 |
260: | E: learned fusion | Logistic regression over the signals and their missing-value indicators, trained on the development set |
261: | Ablations | Hybrid with one signal removed in turn (7.6) |
262: 
263: ### 7.3 Metrics
264: 
265: With one correct answer per query: **Recall@K** (equal to hit rate), **MRR**, **nDCG@K**, and **Precision@K** (capped at 1/K, so reported with that caveat), at K = 1, 3, 5 and 10. **Latency** at the 50th and 95th percentile, at 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000 candidates (synthetic vectors for scale), for approximate and exact search. End-to-end outcomes (verified returns, time to recovery, false claims, unclaimed rate) are operational metrics shown by the dashboard; the benchmark cannot measure them.
266: 
267: ### 7.4 Statistics
268: 
269: Confidence intervals come from a **bootstrap over queries** (1,000 resamples, fixed seed). Differences between systems use a **paired bootstrap** on the same queries. A system is called better only if the 95% interval of the difference excludes 0.
270: 
271: ### 7.5 Protocol and leakage control
272: 
273: Weights and the learned model are chosen on the **development set only**. The chosen configuration is written to a file, hashed, and **frozen**; the test set is evaluated once from that file. The tuning code has no access path to test labels, and a test enforces this. Every run records model names and versions, weights, random seed, dataset hash, git commit and hardware.
274: 
275: ### 7.6 Ablations and robustness
276: 
277: Remove each signal in turn; set 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100% of photos to missing; apply location noise (one level off) and time noise (24 hours off) to 0, 25 and 50% of the found reports. Report each with confidence intervals.
278: 
279: ### 7.7 Honest reporting
280: 
281: Write the hypotheses before the test run (**H1:** the hybrid has a higher MRR than the best single-signal baseline). Report the result whether or not it supports H1. State the limits: synthetic text and location and time rules share assumptions with the scoring function, so any advantage from location and time is partly by construction; the real-photo and human-written subsets are small; and nothing here shows real-world recovery gains.
282:

306: ## 9. API Contract
307: 
308: **Conventions:** JSON over HTTPS; decimals as strings; timestamps in UTC; `limit` (default 20, maximum 100) and an opaque `cursor`; strict request schemas that forbid unknown fields; a resource that is not yours returns **404**, identical to a missing one. Errors are `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}` with 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 410, 413, 415, 422, 423, 429 and 500 used as described in the acceptance criteria.
