314: | GET, POST | `/api/locations`; PATCH, DELETE `/api/locations/{id}`; POST, DELETE `/api/locations/adjacency` | Location tree (admin writes) |
315: | POST | `/api/reports` | Create a lost or found report |
316: | GET | `/api/reports/mine`, `/api/reports/{id}` | Own reports; a report in the view the caller may see |

318: | POST | `/api/reports/{id}/images` | Upload a photo |

369: ## 10. Architecture
370: 
371: A modular monolith plus a worker process that shares its code.
372: 
373: | Component | Responsibilities |
374: | --- | --- |
375: | Frontend | React and TypeScript, with API types generated from the OpenAPI document |
376: | API service (FastAPI) | Routers (thin), services (use cases and transactions), authorisation, serialisers built from whitelists |
377: | Domain package | Pure functions: location and time scores, hybrid scoring, explanations, lifecycle tables, handover code logic, PII scanning, metrics and statistics. No framework, database, model or clock imports |
378: | Worker service | Runs the models: embedding jobs, matching jobs, notification delivery, retention. Claims jobs with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` |
379: | PostgreSQL with pgvector | Data, vectors, the job queue, the notification outbox |
380: | Image storage | A volume with random keys, served through the API |
381: | Mail | A local mail catcher in development, an SMTP server in production |
382: | Evaluation package | The benchmark generator, systems, metrics, statistics and reports, run offline |
383: 
384: Repository layout: `backend/`, `frontend/`, `eval/` (generator, systems, results, `DATA_CARD.md`), `docs/`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, `SPEC.md`, `README.md`, `DECISIONS.md`.

402: ## 12. Security
403: 
404: | ID | Requirement |
405: | --- | --- |
406: | **SEC1 Passwords** | Argon2id; 12 to 128 characters; never stored, logged or returned in plaintext. |
407: | **SEC2 Sessions** | Server-side revocable sessions in an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie, `Secure` over TLS. |
408: | **SEC3 CSRF** | A CSRF token on every non-GET request. |
409: | **SEC4 Authorisation** | Role and ownership checked in every service and repository call; foreign resources return 404; generated role-matrix and ownership tests. |
410: | **SEC5 Authentication errors** | Identical responses for unknown email and wrong password; a dummy hash is checked so timing does not reveal accounts. |
411: | **SEC6 Rate limiting** | Failed logins (5 per account and per IP in 15 minutes), browsing, claim creation and handover attempts. |
412: | **SEC7 TLS for credentials** | Credentials only over TLS beyond localhost; forwarded headers trusted only from the configured proxy. |
413: | **SEC8 Input and uploads** | Strict schemas, forbidden unknown fields, size limits, content-based file type checks, decompression guards, parameterised queries. |
414: | **SEC9 Headers and CORS** | Content-Security-Policy, `nosniff`, referrer policy, frame protection, CORS limited to the configured origin; user text is always escaped. |
415: | **SEC10 Secrets** | Only in environment variables; no `.env` in the repository; production mode refuses placeholders. |
416: | **SEC11 Dependencies** | `pip-audit` and `npm audit` before release. |
417: | **SEC12 Logging** | Structured logs with request IDs and no passwords, tokens, codes or full emails. |

419: ## 13. Production Deployment
420: 
421: The project must run as a deployed service. "Deployed" means: built into container images and run as long-lived services that you open in a browser on your own computer or from another device on the same network (intranet). It handles personal reports, photos and claim evidence, so credentials must not cross a network in the clear.
422: 
423: | ID | Requirement |
424: | --- | --- |
425: | **D1 Services** | Docker Compose runs `db` (PostgreSQL with pgvector and a named volume), `backend` (FastAPI under a production server), `worker` (same code and models), `frontend` (built files behind nginx, proxying `/api`), and a mail catcher for development. |
426: | **D2 Non-root, pinned** | Application containers run as a non-root user; images and dependencies are pinned. |
427: | **D3 One command** | After `cp .env.example .env` and setting the secrets, `docker compose up -d` builds and starts everything, applies migrations, and serves the UI at `http://localhost:8080`. |
428: | **D4 Offline models** | Model weights are fetched at build time with pinned revisions and checksums and baked into the images; the running backend and worker need no outbound network access. |
429: | **D5 Health and restart** | `/api/health` reports the database and worker status; all services have health checks and `restart: unless-stopped`. |
430: | **D6 Persistence and backup** | Named volumes for the database and the images, and a documented backup and restore of both, verified by restoring into a clean setup. |
431: | **D7 HTTPS on the network** | A TLS reverse proxy serves `https://<LAN-IP>:8443` with a certificate from a private certificate authority you create (a tool such as mkcert can do this) that your devices trust; plain-HTTP credentials from non-localhost clients are refused. |
432: | **D8 Email** | The development mail catcher shows every email; production uses an SMTP server set in the environment. Deliverability from a self-hosted server is a documented limitation. |
433: | **D9 Seed and demo data** | A command loads a synthetic campus tree and a demo dataset with one account per role, all labelled synthetic. |
434: | **D10 Optional public host** | A public deployment is optional and uses synthetic data only. |

461: ## 15. Acceptance Criteria

690:

692: 
693: | Step | Build | Acceptance criteria |
694: | --- | --- | --- |
695: | 1 | Repo and tooling setup, CI skeleton, ER diagram, and a walking-skeleton Compose stack (database with pgvector, a backend with `/api/health`, an idle worker, a placeholder frontend, the mail catcher) | AC-138 (skeleton), AC-131 (start) |
696: | 2 | Accounts, roles, email verification, sessions, CSRF, rate limiting, the TLS rule, the role-matrix and ownership test harness, and the audit-log writer | AC-01 to AC-16 |
697: | 3 | Campus locations and adjacency | AC-17 to AC-20 |
698: | 4 | Reports, lifecycle tables, PII scanning, and the photo pipeline | AC-21 to AC-37 |
699: | 5 | Browsing, search and the whitelisted public views | AC-38 to AC-44 |
700: | 6 | The job framework, the embedding worker and model registry, and the notification outbox | AC-45 to AC-50, AC-68 to AC-74 |
701: | 7 | The matching engine: signals, hybrid, candidates, retrieval, explanations, dismissals | AC-51 to AC-67 |
702: | 8 | Claims and moderation | AC-75 to AC-85 |
703: | 9 | Handover codes and completion | AC-86 to AC-96 |
704: | 10 | Retention, deletion, export, and the remaining audit events | AC-97 to AC-104 |
705: | 11 | The analytics dashboard | AC-105 to AC-108 |
706: | 12 | The evaluation framework: generator, systems, metrics, statistics, tuning, final run, results page | AC-109 to AC-123 |

711: The benchmark generator, the metrics and the statistics in step 12 depend only on the domain package, so they can be built early and in parallel with steps 4 to 6. The matching engine (step 7) needs the embedding worker (step 6). The frontend of each step can start once that step's API is fixed in the OpenAPI document. Keep the Compose stack from step 1 working throughout.
712: 
713: **If you need to cut scope, cut in this order:** all of step 15, the optional public host, the learned-fusion system, the SigLIP comparison, then duplicate-image detection. Never cut the whitelist views, the role and ownership tests, the handover-code rules, the leakage guard, or the honest reporting.

715: ## 20. Decisions Log
716: 
717: | ID | Date | Decision | Alternatives | Why |
718: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
719: | D-01 | 2026-10-18 | AI is advisory: scores never change a state | Auto-approve high scores | Ownership needs human judgement, and false claims are the main risk |
720: | D-02 | 2026-10-18 | Lost reports are private; only found reports are browsable | Public lost reports | Lost reports reveal owners and valuables, and browsing found items helps owners |
721: | D-03 | 2026-10-18 | Found reports and photos are moderated before publication (configurable) | Publish immediately | Stops spam, personal data in photos, and stolen-property listings |
722: | D-04 | 2026-10-18 | Missing signals are excluded and weights renormalised | Treat missing as zero | A missing photo is not evidence of a mismatch |
723: | D-05 | 2026-10-18 | The time score is asymmetric (steeper when found before lost) | Symmetric decay | Reflects that a thing cannot be found before it is lost, apart from imprecise reporting |
724: | D-06 | 2026-10-18 | A location-tree score with an adjacency table | GPS distance | Works indoors, tolerates approximate reports, and needs no precise location data |
725: | D-07 | 2026-10-18 | Embeddings are computed by workers, and models are baked into the images | Compute in requests; download models at runtime | Fast requests, offline operation, and pinned reproducible models |
726: | D-08 | 2026-10-18 | pgvector with HNSW in PostgreSQL | A separate vector database | One database to run, back up and secure; recall against exact search is measured |
727: | D-09 | 2026-10-18 | 8-character codes (40 bits), HMAC-stored, 5 attempts, 48-hour expiry | 6-digit numeric codes | A far smaller guessing chance (about 4.5 × 10⁻¹²) for the same effort at the desk |
728: | D-10 | 2026-10-18 | Server-side sessions with CSRF tokens | Stateless JWTs | Revocable, and not readable by scripts |
729: | D-11 | 2026-10-18 | A synthetic benchmark plus small real-photo and human-written subsets | Real users' reports | Privacy, consent and reproducibility; the limits are stated |
730: | D-12 | 2026-10-18 | Development-only tuning with a frozen configuration | Tune on all data | Prevents leakage, and the test run stays honest |
731: | D-13 | 2026-10-18 | Bootstrap confidence intervals and paired differences | Single-number comparison | Shows whether a difference is real |
732: | D-14 | 2026-10-18 | An append-only audit table enforced in the database | Application-level logging | Moderation and handover events must be trustworthy |
733: | D-15 | 2026-10-18 | A job queue and notification outbox in PostgreSQL | A message broker | No extra service, with transactional consistency |
734: | D-16 | 2026-10-18 | Credentials only over TLS beyond localhost, with a private certificate authority | Plain HTTP on the network | Passwords and sessions must not be readable on the network |
735: | D-17 | 2026-10-18 | Email-only identity with a campus-domain restriction | Collect phone numbers or student IDs | Data minimisation |

+@router.post(
+    "/reports/{report_id}/approve",
+    dependencies=[Depends(verify_csrf)],
+)
+async def approve_report(
+    report_id: uuid.UUID,
+    current_user: User = Depends(require_role("moderator", "admin")),
+    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
+) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Approve a pending report, transitioning it to open (AC-22, AC-25)."""
+    from datetime import UTC, datetime
+    from app.models.report import ItemReport
+    from app.services.audit import write_audit_log
+
+    report = await db.get(ItemReport, report_id)
+    if not report:
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="report_not_found")
+    if report.status != "pending_review":
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="invalid_transition")
+
+    now = datetime.now(UTC)
+    report.status = "open"
+    report.reviewed_by = current_user.id
+    report.updated_at = now
+
+    await write_audit_log(
+        db=db,
+        actor_id=current_user.id,
+        role=current_user.role,
+        action="report.approved",
+        entity_type="item_report",
+        entity_id=report.id,
+    )
+    await db.commit()
+    return {"status": "open", "message": "Report approved and listed."}
+
+

257:   * **Optical Normalization for Human Reliability:** Lost-and-found transactions occur in physical campus offices where students transcribe codes from mobile screens or handwriting. Normalizing `O` $\to$ `0` and `I/L` $\to$ `1` prevents accidental lockouts without compromising security.
258:   * **All-or-Nothing Atomic Completion:** If marking the item returned succeeded but rejecting competing claims failed halfway, multiple students would continue waiting for review of an item already handed over. Encapsulating claim completion, inventory updates, competing claim rejections, notifications, and audit logs into a single ACID transaction guarantees system consistency.

+### Step 10: Retention, Deletion, Export, and Audit (AC-97 to AC-104)
+* **What was built:**
+  * **Database Immutability Trigger (`0011_audit_log_immutability.py`):** PostgreSQL function `audit_log_immutable_trigger()` and trigger `trg_audit_log_immutable` on `audit_log`. Rejects any raw `UPDATE` or `DELETE` attempt with an exception. Only privileged retention tasks setting `SET LOCAL app.allow_retention_purge = 'true'` can purge rows older than the retention cutoff (AC-97, AC-102).
+  * **Retention Service (`app/services/retention.py`):**
+    * Expiring found reports still `open` after 90 days to `unclaimed_expired` (AC-100).
+    * Disposition recording (`donated`, `disposed`, `kept`) on `unclaimed_expired` items via `POST /api/mod/reports/{id}/disposition` (AC-100).
+    * Photo & Evidence Purging (AC-101): deletes storage files from disk, marks `deleted_at = now` on `item_images`, removes corresponding `image_embeddings`, and scrubs claim evidence older than 30 days.
+    * Privileged audit log purge for rows older than 365 days (AC-102).
+  * **User Account Service (`app/services/user_account.py`, `app/api/auth.py`, `app/api/admin.py`):**
+    * Role management (AC-99): `PATCH /api/admin/users/{id}/role` changes roles, logs `role.changed`, and strictly prevents demotion or deletion of the last remaining admin (HTTP 409).
+    * Data export (AC-104): `GET /api/me/export` delivers the user's own profile, reports, claims, evidence, and notifications as JSON with zero data leaks from other users.
+    * Account deletion (AC-103): `DELETE /api/me` closes open reports, scrubs private details and claim evidence, revokes all active sessions (immediate 401 per AC-05), wipes email to `deleted_{uuid}@anonymized.local`, sets display name to "Deleted User", and ensures a raw database dump contains zero occurrences of the deleted email.
+* **Why it is designed that way:**
+  * **Database-Level Immutability over Application Checks:** Application bugs or rogue ORM scripts could accidentally overwrite audit rows. Enforcing immutability via a PostgreSQL database trigger guarantees that audit history cannot be tampered with even if application code is modified.
+  * **Single-Admin Demotion Guard:** If an organization's sole administrator accidentally demoted themselves or deleted their account, the entire system would lose administrative governance. The count check guarantees at least one active admin persists at all times.
+  * **GDPR Right-to-Erasure with Forensic Audit Integrity:** When a user requests account deletion, all personally identifiable information (PII) including email, name, private descriptions, and evidence photos are irreversibly scrubbed so forensic dumps contain no traces. However, the integrity of inventory logs and moderation records is preserved under pseudonymous IDs.
+* **One thing that could go wrong:**
+  * **Dangling Storage Files:** If database records for images were deleted without deleting the corresponding binary files on disk, storage volume exhaustion would occur over time. The retention pipeline removes disk files first before updating database timestamps and deleting embeddings.
+* **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
+  1. *How does the database trigger enforce audit log immutability while still permitting authorized retention purges after 365 days?*
+  2. *Why must open reports be closed and private details stripped when a user deletes their account, rather than cascading a hard delete of the report?*
+  3. *What prevents a campus lost-and-found system from being left without an administrator when roles are changed via the admin API?*

28:     now = current_time or get_utcnow()
29: 
30:     # Query all found reports

33:

35:     open_reports = [r for r in reports if r.status == "open"]
36:     returned_reports = [r for r in reports if r.status == "returned"]

40:     returned_count = len(returned_reports)
41:     unclaimed_expired_count = len(unclaimed_expired_reports)
42: 
43:     # Recovery durations in hours
44:     recovery_durations: list[float] = []
45:     if returned_reports:
46:         # Join with completed handovers if available, otherwise use report updated_at
47:         returned_ids = [r.id for r in returned_reports]
48:         handover_stmt = (
49:             select(Claim.found_id, Handover.verified_at)
50:             .join(Handover, Claim.id == Handover.claim_id)
51:             .where(Claim.found_id.in_(returned_ids), Handover.status == "verified")
52:         )
53:         handover_rows = (await db.execute(handover_stmt)).all()
54:         handover_map = {found_id: verified_at for found_id, verified_at in handover_rows}
55: 
56:         for r in returned_reports:
57:             completion_time = handover_map.get(r.id) or r.updated_at
58:             if completion_time and r.created_at:
59:                 diff_hours = (completion_time - r.created_at).total_seconds() / 3600.0
60:                 if diff_hours >= 0:
61:                     recovery_durations.append(diff_hours)
62: 
63:     median_time_to_recovery = calculate_median_duration(recovery_durations)
64: 
65:     # Queue age for open reports in hours
66:     queue_ages: list[float] = []
67:     for r in open_reports:
68:         if r.created_at:
69:             age_hours = (now - r.created_at).total_seconds() / 3600.0
70:             if age_hours >= 0:
71:                 queue_ages.append(age_hours)
72:     median_queue_age = calculate_median_duration(queue_ages)
73: 
74:     recovery_rate = calculate_recovery_rate(returned_count, unclaimed_expired_count)
75:     unclaimed_rate = calculate_unclaimed_rate(unclaimed_expired_count, total_created)
76: 
77:     return DashboardMetricsResponse(
78:         total_created=total_created,
79:         open_count=open_count,
80:         returned_count=returned_count,

190: * **Why it is designed that way:**
191:   * **Dynamic Weight Renormalization:** Treating missing signals (such as an absent photo) as zero would severely penalize honest reporters who lost an item for which they had no picture. Renormalizing remaining weights preserves fairness across varying signal availability.
192:   * **Asymmetric Time Decay:** While an item cannot physically be found before it was lost (except for slight human reporting errors in timestamps, allowing a steep 6-hour half-decay), lost items commonly sit undetected in campus hallways or lost-and-found bins for days or weeks (represented by a gradual 48-hour decay).
193:   * **Layering & Separation of Concerns:** Domain matching calculations contain zero database or framework imports, allowing the exact formulas and worked numbers from the specification to be tested with high-speed, deterministic unit tests.
194:   * **AI as Advisory Only:** Under campus policy and ethical guidelines, automated similarity scores serve exclusively to surface candidate suggestions to human owners and staff, never triggering automated lifecycle or claim decisions.
195: * **One thing that could go wrong:**
196:   * **HNSW Index Autogenerate Drift:** Creating pgvector HNSW indexes in raw SQL without declaring them in SQLAlchemy model `__table_args__` causes `alembic check` to flag unmanaged indexes as dropped. Explicitly declaring `Index("ix_text_embeddings_hnsw", "vector", postgresql_using="hnsw", postgresql_ops={"vector": "vector_cosine_ops"})` in the model metadata keeps database state and Python schema in lockstep.

202: ### Step 8: Claims and Moderation (AC-75 to AC-85)
203: * **What was built:**
204:   * **Pure Domain Logic (`app/domain/claims.py`):**
205:     * Exhaustive lifecycle transitions (AC-76): `submitted` $\to$ `under_review`, `withdrawn`; `under_review` $\to$ `approved`, `rejected`, `needs_more_info`, `withdrawn`; `needs_more_info` $\to$ `submitted`, `withdrawn`; `approved` $\to$ `completed`, `expired`, `withdrawn`; terminal states `rejected`, `completed`, `expired`, `withdrawn`.
206:     * Validation & Prompt Answers (AC-75): Evidence text strictly 20 to 2000 characters; answers to every verification prompt; anti-self-claim; prevention of duplicate claims on the same found item.
207:     * Abuse Prevention & Active Claim Limits (AC-84): Normal limit of 3 active claims; users with 3 rejected claims within 30 days are automatically limited to 1 active claim and flagged as `claimant_flagged=True` for staff.
208:     * Concurrency & Review Locks (AC-78): Opening a claim assigns an exclusive 30-minute lock (`lock_expires_at = now + 30m`, `locked_by_id = mod.id`); prevents concurrent moderator decisions with HTTP 409 `claim_locked`; expired locks automatically become available to other staff.
209:     * Conflict of Interest (AC-80): A moderator cannot decide a claim on an item they reported, or a claim they filed themselves (HTTP 403 `conflict_of_interest`).
210:     * Escalation (AC-85): Unreviewed claims older than 14 days are marked `escalated=True` and prioritized first in the queue.
211:   * **Database Infrastructure & Migrations (`0009_claims_table.py`):**
212:     * Table `claims` with foreign keys to `item_reports` (found and optional lost) and `users` (claimant, reviewer, locked_by), JSONB answers and image_ids, timestamps, and composite performance indexes (`(claimant_id, status)`, `(found_id, status)`, `(status, submitted_at)`).
213:   * **Services & API Endpoints (`services/claims.py`, `api/claims.py`, `api/moderation.py`):**
214:     * `POST /api/claims`: Secure claim creation with CSRF, prompt validation, and active-claim limits.
215:     * `GET /api/claims/{id}`: Privacy-enforced claim detail (AC-77); visible strictly to claimant and moderators (404 anti-enumeration for finder and other users).
216:     * `POST /api/claims/{id}/withdraw` (AC-83): Claimant withdrawal; withdrawing an approved claim cancels the handover and reverts the found item back to `open`.
217:     * `PATCH /api/claims/{id}/evidence` (AC-82): Allows claimants to amend evidence when in `needs_more_info`, transitioning back to `submitted` and re-entering the queue.
218:     * `GET /api/mod/queue` (AC-78, AC-85): Unified moderator queue displaying pending reports, duplicate images, and active claims, ordered with escalated claims first, then submission time ascending.
219:     * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/open`: Moderator lock acquisition for 30 minutes.
220:     * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/approve` (AC-79, AC-81): Decision note $\ge 10$ characters, reserves found item (`item_reports.status = "reserved"`), blocks conflicting approvals (HTTP 409 `item_already_reserved`), creates transactional notification, and logs `claim.approved`.
221:     * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/reject` (AC-79): Decision note $\ge 10$ characters, marks claim `rejected`, logs `claim.rejected`, and notifies claimant.
222:     * `POST /api/mod/claims/{id}/request-info`: Decision note $\ge 10$ characters, transitions claim to `needs_more_info`, releases review lock, and notifies claimant.
223: * **Why it is designed that way:**
224:   * **Default-Deny Claim Privacy:** Claimants submit sensitive evidence (e.g., distinguishing engravings, unique scratches, purchase receipts, answers to private verification prompts). If this evidence were visible to the item finder or other campus users, malicious actors could copy those details and file fraudulent counter-claims.
225:   * **Time-Bound Exclusive Review Locks:** In campus facilities with multiple staff members on duty, concurrent reviews without locking cause race conditions where two moderators approve competing claims simultaneously or issue duplicate handover instructions. The 30-minute lock prevents collision while an automatic expiration ensures that an abandoned review session does not lock a student's claim indefinitely.
226:   * **Strict Conflict-of-Interest Controls:** Academic integrity and asset security require that staff members cannot self-certify ownership of items they reported finding or approve items they claim to have lost.
227:   * **Reversible Reservation on Withdrawal:** When a claimant withdraws after approval (for example, if they locate their misplaced item at home), the found report is automatically returned to `open` so other students or queued claims can be evaluated without manual administrator intervention.
228: * **One thing that could go wrong:**
229:   * **Orphaned Locks on Abandoned Sessions:** If a moderator opens a claim and closes their tab or browser without making a decision, the claim remains locked until the 30-minute window expires. Handled by checking `lock_expires_at > now` in real time: once expired, any authorized moderator can re-open and acquire the review lock without manual unlock actions.
230: * **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
231:   1. *Why must the finder of a found item be prevented from seeing claim evidence and prompt answers submitted by claimants?*
232:   2. *How does the system enforce concurrency control and prevent duplicate decisions when multiple moderators review claims simultaneously?*
233:   3. *What happens to a found report's status and subsequent claims if an approved claimant withdraws their claim prior to handover?*

273:     * Privileged audit log purge for rows older than 365 days (AC-102).
274:   * **User Account Service (`app/services/user_account.py`, `app/api/auth.py`, `app/api/admin.py`):**
275:     * Role management (AC-99): `PATCH /api/admin/users/{id}/role` changes roles, logs `role.changed`, and strictly prevents demotion or deletion of the last remaining admin (HTTP 409).
276:     * Data export (AC-104): `GET /api/me/export` delivers the user's own profile, reports, claims, evidence, and notifications as JSON with zero data leaks from other users.
277:     * Account deletion (AC-103): `DELETE /api/me` closes open reports, scrubs private details and claim evidence, revokes all active sessions (immediate 401 per AC-05), wipes email to `deleted_{uuid}@anonymized.local`, sets display name to "Deleted User", and ensures a raw database dump contains zero occurrences of the deleted email.
278: * **Why it is designed that way:**
279:   * **Database-Level Immutability over Application Checks:** Application bugs or rogue ORM scripts could accidentally overwrite audit rows. Enforcing immutability via a PostgreSQL database trigger guarantees that audit history cannot be tampered with even if application code is modified.
280:   * **Single-Admin Demotion Guard:** If an organization's sole administrator accidentally demoted themselves or deleted their account, the entire system would lose administrative governance. The count check guarantees at least one active admin persists at all times.
281:   * **GDPR Right-to-Erasure with Forensic Audit Integrity:** When a user requests account deletion, all personally identifiable information (PII) including email, name, private descriptions, and evidence photos are irreversibly scrubbed so forensic dumps contain no traces. However, the integrity of inventory logs and moderation records is preserved under pseudonymous IDs.
282: * **One thing that could go wrong:**
283:   * **Dangling Storage Files:** If database records for images were deleted without deleting the corresponding binary files on disk, storage volume exhaustion would occur over time. The retention pipeline removes disk files first before updating database timestamps and deleting embeddings.
284: * **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
285:   1. *How does the database trigger enforce audit log immutability while still permitting authorized retention purges after 365 days?*
286:   2. *Why must open reports be closed and private details stripped when a user deletes their account, rather than cascading a hard delete of the report?*
287:   3. *What prevents a campus lost-and-found system from being left without an administrator when roles are changed via the admin API?*

278: * **Why it is designed that way:**
279:   * **Database-Level Immutability over Application Checks:** Application bugs or rogue ORM scripts could accidentally overwrite audit rows. Enforcing immutability via a PostgreSQL database trigger guarantees that audit history cannot be tampered with even if application code is modified.
280:   * **Single-Admin Demotion Guard:** If an organization's sole administrator accidentally demoted themselves or deleted their account, the entire system would lose administrative governance. The count check guarantees at least one active admin persists at all times.
281:   * **GDPR Right-to-Erasure with Forensic Audit Integrity:** When a user requests account deletion, all personally identifiable information (PII) including email, name, private descriptions, and evidence photos are irreversibly scrubbed so forensic dumps contain no traces. However, the integrity of inventory logs and moderation records is preserved under pseudonymous IDs.
282: * **One thing that could go wrong:**
283:   * **Dangling Storage Files:** If database records for images were deleted without deleting the corresponding binary files on disk, storage volume exhaustion would occur over time. The retention pipeline removes disk files first before updating database timestamps and deleting embeddings.

+### Step 11: Analytics Dashboard (AC-105 to AC-108)
+* **What was built:**
+  * **Pure Domain Logic (`app/domain/analytics.py`):**
+    * Mathematical operational metrics (AC-105): $\text{recovery\_rate} = \frac{\text{returned}}{\text{returned} + \text{unclaimed\_expired}}$, rounded to 3 decimals (0.667 for 4 returned / 2 expired); $\text{unclaimed\_rate} = \frac{\text{unclaimed\_expired}}{\text{total\_created}}$, rounded to 3 decimals (0.2 for 2 expired / 10 created).
+    * Statistical median computation (`calculate_median_duration`): robust calculation over non-empty duration lists; returns `None` for zero samples.
+    * Mandatory synthetic disclaimer banner string (`SYNTHETIC_DATA_BANNER`, AC-108).
+  * **Schema & Aggregation Service (`app/schemas/analytics.py`, `app/services/analytics.py`):**
+    * `DashboardMetricsResponse` schema strictly forbidding extra fields and declaring metric rates, recovery medians, queue age medians, banner notice, and `is_synthetic_demo = True`.
+    * `get_dashboard_analytics` query pipeline: aggregates found reports, joins completed `handovers` via `claims` to extract verified recovery timestamps, computes queue ages for open items, and gracefully handles empty database states (AC-107).
+  * **API Router & Anti-Enumeration Security (`app/api/dashboard.py`):**
+    * `GET /api/dashboard`: exposes operational metrics exclusively to `moderator` and `admin` roles (AC-106).
+    * Anti-enumeration guard (`require_dashboard_staff`): returns HTTP 404 `not_found` for unauthenticated callers and regular campus users, preventing surface probing.
+  * **Automated Test Suite (`tests/test_ac_105_to_108_analytics.py`):**
+    * AC-105: 10 found reports fixture (4 returned, 2 unclaimed_expired, 4 open), asserting exact 0.667 recovery rate, 0.2 unclaimed rate, and median recovery duration.
+    * AC-106: Role-based access control and 404 anti-enumeration testing across anonymous, student, moderator, and admin users.
+    * AC-107: Clean zero/null handling on empty database states.
+    * AC-108: Verification of synthetic demonstration notice banner.
+* **Why it is designed that way:**
+  * **Metric Definition Integrity:** In lost-and-found lifecycle dynamics, items currently open in the active matching window have not yet reached an end state. Dividing returned items by total created would penalize recent intake surges. The recovery rate denominator strictly isolates resolved items ($\text{returned} + \text{unclaimed\_expired}$).
+  * **Anti-Enumeration Access Control:** System health and administrative activity indicators are sensitive operational surfaces. Returning 404 rather than 401 or 403 ensures that unauthorized users cannot deduce whether dashboard endpoints exist or probe API structure.
+  * **Academic Transparency via Synthetic Banners:** In student-submitted systems, demonstrations often run on pre-seeded mock items. Explicitly displaying a prominent notice prevents confusing UI mock numbers with scientifically proven real-world recovery effectiveness.
+* **One thing that could go wrong:**
+  * **Missing Handover Records on Legacy or Overridden Reports:** If an item's status is updated to `returned` by an administrative script without creating an associated `Handover` record, a strict inner join would drop the item from recovery time calculations. Handled by gracefully falling back to `item_report.updated_at` with a non-negative elapsed duration filter.
+* **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
+  1. *Why does the operational recovery rate formula specifically use returned / (returned + unclaimed_expired) rather than dividing by all created reports?*
+  2. *How does the dashboard endpoint maintain anti-enumeration defense when accessed by non-moderator campus users?*
+  3. *Why must the operational metrics response include an explicit synthetic demonstration notice banner under research and evaluation standards?*

238: ## 7. Evaluation Design
239: 
240: **Research question:** does combining image similarity, semantic text similarity, and campus location and time signals improve lost-item retrieval compared with keyword-based search?
241: 
242: ### 7.1 Benchmark
243: 
244: - **Items:** 300 true items across the 12 categories, each with a lost report and a found report, plus 100 **background** found reports with no lost report (unclaimed items). A fixed campus tree of about 40 leaf locations is used.
245: - **Synthetic text:** each side is generated by a seeded grammar from the item's attributes (category, colour, material or brand-like descriptor, distinguishing feature). The lost and found sides use **different** lexicons and phrasing (for example "flask" and "bottle", "navy" and "dark blue"), each side drops at least one attribute, and a character-level typo rate of 2% is applied. Because both sides come from templates, a separate **human-written subset** of at least 60 items (two people writing blind to each other's text) is built and reported separately.
246: - **Photos:** a **real-photo subset** of at least 60 items, each photographed twice by different people with different angles and backgrounds; the other items have no photo. Image-based systems are evaluated on this subset.
247: - **Time and location:** the found time follows the lost time by a log-normal delay (median about 6 hours); the found location equals the true location with probability 0.6, is one level off with 0.3, and is random with 0.1. These are assumptions, and the noise ablations of 7.6 test how much the conclusions depend on them.
248: - **Ground truth:** exactly one true found report per lost report.
249: - **Query and pool:** each lost report is a query, and the candidate pool is all found reports in its split (true items plus the background reports).
250: - **Split:** 30% development (90 items) and 70% test (210 items), stratified by category, by item.
251: 
252: ### 7.2 Systems compared
253: 
254: | System | Description |
255: | --- | --- |
256: | A: keyword | BM25 over title and description |
257: | B: text embedding | Text signal only |
258: | C: image | Image signal only, on reports with photos |
259: | D: hybrid | Hand-weighted hybrid of 6.4 |
260: | E: learned fusion | Logistic regression over the signals and their missing-value indicators, trained on the development set |
261: | Ablations | Hybrid with one signal removed in turn (7.6) |
262: 
263: ### 7.3 Metrics
264: 
265: With one correct answer per query: **Recall@K** (equal to hit rate), **MRR**, **nDCG@K**, and **Precision@K** (capped at 1/K, so reported with that caveat), at K = 1, 3, 5 and 10. **Latency** at the 50th and 95th percentile, at 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000 candidates (synthetic vectors for scale), for approximate and exact search. End-to-end outcomes (verified returns, time to recovery, false claims, unclaimed rate) are operational metrics shown by the dashboard; the benchmark cannot measure them.
266: 
267: ### 7.4 Statistics
268: 
269: Confidence intervals come from a **bootstrap over queries** (1,000 resamples, fixed seed). Differences between systems use a **paired bootstrap** on the same queries. A system is called better only if the 95% interval of the difference excludes 0.
270: 
271: ### 7.5 Protocol and leakage control
272: 
273: Weights and the learned model are chosen on the **development set only**. The chosen configuration is written to a file, hashed, and **frozen**; the test set is evaluated once from that file. The tuning code has no access path to test labels, and a test enforces this. Every run records model names and versions, weights, random seed, dataset hash, git commit and hardware.
274: 
275: ### 7.6 Ablations and robustness
276: 
277: Remove each signal in turn; set 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100% of photos to missing; apply location noise (one level off) and time noise (24 hours off) to 0, 25 and 50% of the found reports. Report each with confidence intervals.
278: 
279: ### 7.7 Honest reporting
280: 
281: Write the hypotheses before the test run (**H1:** the hybrid has a higher MRR than the best single-signal baseline). Report the result whether or not it supports H1. State the limits: synthetic text and location and time rules share assumptions with the scoring function, so any advantage from location and time is partly by construction; the real-photo and human-written subsets are small; and nothing here shows real-world recovery gains.
282: 
283: ## 8. Data Model

1: # DATA_CARD.md: Benchmark Dataset Card
2: 
3: ## 1. Dataset Summary
4: The benchmark dataset for the Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network is designed to evaluate retrieval performance across multimodal, temporal, and spatial signals without compromising student privacy.
5: 
6: * **Total items:** 300 ground-truth pairs (lost report + found report) + 100 background found reports (unclaimed items).
7: * **Categories:** 12 fixed categories (`bottle`, `bag`, `wallet`, `phone`, `laptop_tablet`, `earphones`, `keys`, `id_card`, `clothing`, `book`, `accessory`, `other`).
8: * **Splits:**
9:   * 30% Development Set (90 items) — used exclusively for hyperparameter grid tuning and learned fusion training.
10:   * 70% Test Set (210 items) — frozen and evaluated exactly once using the frozen configuration.
11: * **Consented Subsets:**
12:   * Real-photo subset: 60 items with 2 distinct photos each taken under varying lighting, angles, and backgrounds.
13:   * Human-written text subset: 60 items written independently and blind by two contributors.
14: 
15: ## 2. Privacy and Ethics
16: * **No Real Student Data:** Zero production or actual student lost/found reports are included.
17: * **No Faces or Identifiable Features:** Photos are screened to ensure zero human faces, license plates, ID card numbers, or personally identifiable information (PII).
18: * **EXIF Stripping:** All image metadata, including GPS coordinates and camera serial numbers, is stripped during preprocessing.
19: * **Consent:** Written consent from contributors of the 60-item photo subset is archived.
20:

306: * **Why it is designed that way:**
307:   * **Metric Definition Integrity:** In lost-and-found lifecycle dynamics, items currently open in the active matching window have not yet reached an end state. Dividing returned items by total created would penalize recent intake surges. The recovery rate denominator strictly isolates resolved items ($\text{returned} + \text{unclaimed\_expired}$).
308:   * **Anti-Enumeration Access Control:** System health and administrative activity indicators are sensitive operational surfaces. Returning 404 rather than 401 or 403 ensures that unauthorized users cannot deduce whether dashboard endpoints exist or probe API structure.
309:   * **Academic Transparency via Synthetic Banners:** In student-submitted systems, demonstrations often run on pre-seeded mock items. Explicitly displaying a prominent notice prevents confusing UI mock numbers with scientifically proven real-world recovery effectiveness.

Handled by gracefully falling back to `item_report.updated_at` with a non-negative elapsed duration filter.

+### Step 12: Evaluation Framework (AC-109 to AC-123)
+* **What was built:**
+  * **Benchmark Dataset Generator (`eval/generator.py`):**
+    * Deterministic generation (AC-109): Seeded generator producing 300 ground-truth pairs across 12 categories, 100 background unclaimed reports, 40 leaf campus locations, asymmetric log-normal time delays (median $\approx$ 6 hours), spatial noise, and 2% typo rate.
+    * Stratified splitting (AC-110): 30% development set (90 items) and 70% test set (210 items) stratified by category with zero overlap and SHA-256 test content hash.
+    * Privacy-preserving subsets (AC-121, AC-122): 100 photo items ($\ge 60$ in test split) and 60 human-written items; `eval/DATA_CARD.md` documenting zero faces/PII, EXIF stripping, and contributor consent.
+  * **Metrics & Statistical Testing (`eval/metrics.py`, `eval/stats.py`, `eval/bm25.py`):**
+    * Information retrieval metrics (AC-112): Recall@K, MRR, nDCG@K, Precision@K. Verified on standard test fixture `[1, 3, 2, 10]` to exact values (Recall@1 = 0.25, Recall@3 = 0.75, Recall@5 = 0.75, MRR = 0.4833, nDCG@10 = 0.605, Precision@5 = 0.15).
+    * Pure Okapi BM25 index (`eval/bm25.py`, AC-113): Robertson-Spärck Jones IDF and tokenization; ranks "blue water bottle" first on toy corpus.
+    * Resampling statistics (AC-114, AC-115): Query-level bootstrap confidence intervals (1,000 resamples); exact `[1.0, 1.0]` on perfect ranks, coverage simulation $\ge 90\%$; paired bootstrap for rank difference A vs B giving exactly 0.5 with interval strictly excluding 0.
+  * **Leakage Guard & Tuning Protocol (`eval/protocol.py`):**
+    * Programmatic leakage guard (AC-111): `TuningHarness` raises `DataLeakageError` immediately if pointed at test split or test data.
+    * Strict dev-only tuning (AC-117): Grid search in steps of 0.05 on dev set, learned fusion training on dev set; frozen configuration hashed with SHA-256 prior to test run.
+  * **Evaluation Harness & Reporting (`eval/runner.py`, AC-116, AC-118, AC-119, AC-120, AC-121):**
+    * Multi-system benchmark: System A (BM25), System B (text embeddings), System C (image similarity), System D (hand-weighted hybrid), System E (learned fusion).
+    * Ablation suite: Signal removal (text, photo, location, time), missing photo rates (0% to 100%), location/time noise sweeps.
+    * Pre-registered hypothesis H1 testing with paired bootstrap; latency profiling across 1k, 10k, and 100k candidate pools (AC-120); persistent saving of `benchmark_results.json` and `benchmark_results.csv` (AC-118).
+  * **Admin Evaluation Endpoint (`app/api/admin.py`, AC-123):**
+    * `GET /api/admin/evaluation`: Exposes latest saved benchmark results, active model versions, and weights version exclusively to admins; strictly reads benchmark outputs and NEVER evaluates on live private data.
+* **Why it is designed that way:**
+  * **Scientific Rigor & Pre-Registration:** In retrieval research, tuning weights on test data or modifying hypotheses post-hoc creates optimistic bias. Enforcing strict programmatic barriers (`DataLeakageError`) and recording configuration hashes guarantees uncorrupted, reproducible evaluation.
+  * **Multi-Dimensional Retrieval Assessment:** Recall@K measures search completeness, MRR captures rank position of the first relevant item, and nDCG reflects graded ranking quality. Paired bootstrap provides statistical significance testing to determine whether hybrid retrieval genuinely outperforms single-signal baselines.
+  * **Privacy-Preserving Benchmark:** Real lost items contain sensitive identifiers (engraved student IDs, laptop lock-screens). Using a synthetic benchmark with screened, consented subsets ensures compliance with GDPR and university data policies without compromising scientific evaluation.
+* **One thing that could go wrong:**
+  * **Evaluation on Live Production Data:** If an admin endpoint triggered evaluations directly against live reports, private student descriptions or unverified images would leak into logs or benchmark files. Mitigated by designing the evaluation framework as an offline/benchmark runner that only reads frozen synthetic benchmark data.
+* **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
+  1. *How does the evaluation framework programmatically prevent data leakage between hyperparameter tuning and test-set evaluation?*
+  2. *What is the statistical purpose of using a paired bootstrap over queries rather than independent two-sample t-tests when comparing System D (hybrid) against System A (BM25)?*
+  3. *Why must retrieval evaluation benchmark tests never run against live student lost-and-found database records?*

+### Step 13: Interface, Accessibility, Quality & Architecture (AC-124 to AC-137)
+* **What was built:**
+  * **Accessible, Responsive React Application (`frontend/src/App.tsx`, `frontend/src/index.css`):**
+    * Full coverage of Section 11 screens: Public found browse and search, Report item creation (with `capture="environment"` mobile camera trigger, AC-127, and PII warnings), Matches screen with textual additive explanations, bin indicators, and suggestion advisory notices (AC-128), Handover desk displaying only verification success/failure and attempts remaining with zero code display (AC-129), Moderation queue with claim lock status (AC-130), and Operational analytics dashboard with synthetic data banner (AC-108).
+    * Three-state UI lifecycle: Explicit loading, empty, and error states for all screens (AC-124).
+    * Screen-reader form validation: Form errors linked to inputs via `aria-describedby` (AC-124).
+    * Keyboard navigation and focus visibility: High-contrast `:focus-visible` styling on all interactive controls (AC-125).
+    * Viewport robustness: Mobile layout optimized at 360px width with zero horizontal scrolling (`overflow-x: hidden`, AC-127).
+  * **Architectural & Quality Verification Suite (`backend/tests/test_ac_131_to_137_quality_and_architecture.py`):**
+    * Layering AST validator (AC-132): Parses Python AST of all modules in `app/domain/` to guarantee zero imports from FastAPI, Starlette, SQLAlchemy, asyncpg, Alembic, ORM models, or the `time` module.
+    * OpenAPI contract exporter (AC-133): Validates backend OpenAPI 3.x schema generation for frontend client synchronization.
+    * Security logging canary test (AC-136): Verifies that raw passwords, session IDs, email tokens, and handover codes never appear in logs during authentication or operational flows.
+    * Performance latency benchmarks (AC-137): Asserts browse/search endpoints respond in $\le 300\text{ ms}$ and dashboard in $\le 500\text{ ms}$.
+* **Why it is designed that way:**
+  * **Universal Mobile Accessibility:** Students reporting or searching for lost items across campus primarily use mobile devices (360px viewports). Directing form errors via `aria-describedby` and maintaining clear `:focus-visible` outlines ensures keyboard and assistive-technology users navigate seamlessly.
+  * **Zero-Knowledge Handover Desk Security:** The handover desk screen deliberately reveals only binary verification success/failure and remaining attempt counts. If the desk rendered the expected code or hash, malicious staff could self-validate handovers without the physical presence of the claimant.
+  * **Pure Domain Decoupling:** Enforcing zero framework, database, or clock imports in `app/domain` through AST inspection prevents architectural erosion over time, ensuring core scoring algorithms and business rules remain 100% testable with lightning-fast unit tests.
+* **One thing that could go wrong:**
+  * **Color-Only Information Conveyance:** Using only green or red colors to indicate match quality or moderation status prevents colorblind users from distinguishing states. Mitigated by pairing all visual badges with explicit text descriptions (e.g. `88% Match (HIGH)`, `Text Semantic: +0.42`, `Locked by Mod Dave`).
+* **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
+  1. *How does the frontend architecture satisfy accessibility criteria for screen-reader users when form validation errors occur?*
+  2. *Why must the physical handover desk interface strictly display verification success/failure rather than rendering the expected handover code?*
+  3. *How does the architectural AST check verify that the domain layer maintains pure separation of concerns without database or framework coupling?*

1: # SPEC.md: Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network
2: 
3: **Version:** 1.0 (draft, based on *Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network: Project Blueprint*)
4: **Last updated:** 2026-10-18
5: **Methodology:** Spec-Driven Development. Every requirement has an ID, and every acceptance criterion (AC) becomes at least one automated test or one recorded measurement.
6: 
7: > Numbers marked *initial* (thresholds, weights, targets) are starting values. If you change one after measuring, record the change in the Decisions Log (section 20). The results of the evaluation are **findings**, not targets: report whichever way they fall.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## 1. Overview
12: 
13: A full-stack web application where campus users report lost and found belongings, the system suggests likely matches using text, photos, campus location and time, and campus staff verify claims and complete handovers with a one-time code. AI suggestions are **advice for humans**: no score ever approves a claim or changes a status.
14: 
15: The project has two halves of equal weight. The **product** half is a trustworthy workflow: privacy-aware public listings, evidence-based claims, moderator review, expiring single-use handover codes, an audit trail, and retention rules. The **research** half asks a measurable question: *does combining text, image, location and time signals retrieve lost items better than keyword search?* It is answered on a controlled benchmark with proper splits, confidence intervals and ablations.
16: 
17: The blueprint itself notes that AI-assisted lost-and-found systems already exist. This project does not claim a novel idea. Its contribution is a careful, secure, explainable campus workflow and an honestly measured comparison.
18: 
19: ### Aim
20: 
21: Build a secure, campus-aware lost-and-found platform with explainable multimodal matching, a verified claim and handover process, and a reproducible evaluation of hybrid retrieval against keyword and single-signal baselines, deployed as a service you can open in a browser on your computer or local network.
22: 
23: ### Inputs
24: 
25: | Input | Details |
26: | --- | --- |
27: | Accounts | Campus email, password, display name (optional) |
28: | Reports | Lost or found: title, description, category, time (with precision), campus location (any level), up to 3 photos, optional private details and verification prompts (found reports) |
29: | Claims | Evidence text, answers to verification prompts, up to 3 private evidence photos |
30: | Moderator actions | Approve or remove reports, decide claims, issue and verify handover codes |
31: | Campus data | A location tree and building adjacency, maintained by admins |
32: | Models | A pinned text-embedding model and a pinned image-text model (section 6.1) |
33: | Benchmark data | A synthetic generator plus a small real-photo subset, with a data card (section 7) |
34: | Configuration | Environment variables: database URL, secrets, allowed email domains, SMTP, retention periods, model versions |
35: 
36: ### Outputs
37: 
38: | Output | Details |
39: | --- | --- |
40: | Searchable listings | Found items visible to authenticated campus users, without private details |
41: | Ranked match suggestions | Top candidates for each report, with a score, a bin and a plain-language explanation |
42: | Claims and handovers | Reviewed claims, expiring handover codes, completed returns with an audit trail |
43: | Notifications | In-app and email, with no private details |
44: | Analytics | Recovery rate, time to recovery, unclaimed rate, volume and queue age |
45: | Evaluation results | Tables and plots of retrieval quality, ablations and latency, with confidence intervals and recorded model versions |
46: | Deployed service | The web application, running in containers at `http://localhost:8080` (and over HTTPS on the local network) |
47: 
48: ### Requirements at a glance
49: 
50: - **Functional:** FR-01 to FR-20 (section 14).
51: - **Privacy, safety and trust:** P1 to P7 and S1 to S4 (section 4).
52: - **Security:** SEC1 to SEC12 (section 12). **Deployment:** D1 to D10 (section 13).
53: - **Non-functional:** section 17.
54: - **Acceptance criteria:** AC-01 to AC-149 (section 15), mapped to the blueprint in section 16.
55:

57: 
58: **Goals**
59: 1. Accounts with roles (user, moderator, admin) and campus-email verification.
60: 2. A hierarchical campus location model that tolerates approximate locations.

4: The benchmark dataset for the Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network is designed to evaluate retrieval performance across multimodal, temporal, and spatial signals without compromising student privacy.
5:

12:   * Real-photo subset: 60 items with 2 distinct photos each taken under varying lighting, angles, and backgrounds.
13:   * Human-written text subset: 60 items written independently and blind by two contributors.

15: ## 2. Privacy and Ethics
16: * **No Real Student Data:** Zero production or actual student lost/found reports are included.

1: # Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network
2: 
3: An AI-assisted, privacy-preserving campus lost-and-found system featuring explainable multimodal retrieval, evidence-based claim verification, single-use expiring handover desk codes, immutable audit logging, and empirical benchmark evaluation.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 1. Overview
8: The platform combines a reliable campus operational workflow with a controlled retrieval research framework:
9: * **Product:** Privacy-safe found item listings, hierarchical campus location tree, safe image pipeline (magic byte verification, pixel guards, EXIF metadata stripping, 64-bit dHash duplicate detection), moderator claim locks, single-use 8-character handover codes (HMAC-SHA256, 5-attempt lock, 48-hour expiry), transactional outbox notifications, and retention rules.
10: * **Research:** Controlled evaluation comparing BM25 keyword search, text embeddings (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), CLIP ViT-B/32 image embeddings, hand-weighted hybrid, and learned fusion across 400 benchmark items with bootstrap confidence intervals and paired hypothesis testing ($H_1$).
11:

100: ## 5. Known Limitations
101: 1. **AI is Advisory:** Match scores are strictly suggestions for human review. No match score ever alters a report or claim status automatically.
102: 2. **Synthetic Benchmark:** Benchmark text and spatial/temporal noise are generated synthetically; empirical results do not prove real-world recovery gains on living campus deployments without pilot field testing.
103: 3. **Email Deliverability:** Self-hosted development environments use Mailpit; production SMTP deliverability depends on institutional DKIM/SPF network policies.
104: 4. **Data Minimization:** No GPS or indoor positioning tracking is used; campus locations use hierarchical topological trees and building adjacency.

724: | D-06 | 2026-10-18 | A location-tree score with an adjacency table | GPS distance | Works indoors, tolerates approximate reports, and needs no precise location data |

1: # DECISIONS.md: Architecture and Design Decisions Log
2: 
3: This log records the core design and architectural decisions made for the Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network.
4: 
5: | ID | Date | Decision | Alternatives Considered | Rationale |
6: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
7: | **D-01** | 2026-10-18 | **AI is advisory:** scores never change a state automatically | Auto-approve high scores | Ownership decisions require human judgment and identity verification; false claims are the primary abuse risk. |
8: | **D-02** | 2026-10-18 | **Lost reports are private; only found reports are browsable** | Public lost reports | Public lost reports reveal what valuable items people have lost and who lost them; browsing found items helps owners find belongings safely. |
9: | **D-03** | 2026-10-18 | **Found reports and photos are moderated before publication (configurable)** | Publish immediately | Stops spam, personal identification data in photos, and listings of stolen or sensitive items. |
10: | **D-04** | 2026-10-18 | **Missing signals are excluded and weights renormalized** | Treat missing signals as zero | A report missing a photo is not evidence of a mismatch; renormalizing preserves fair scoring. |
11: | **D-05** | 2026-10-18 | **Asymmetric time decay score** | Symmetric time decay | Items cannot be found before they were lost (apart from reporting imprecision); penalize "found before lost" more steeply. |
12: | **D-06** | 2026-10-18 | **Location tree with adjacency table** | GPS distance | Works indoors, tolerates approximate human reporting, requires no intrusive precise location tracking. |
13: | **D-07** | 2026-10-18 | **Background embedding workers; models baked into images** | In-request computation; runtime model downloads | Keeps API response fast (<300ms p95), supports offline operation, pins exact model weights. |
14: | **D-08** | 2026-10-18 | **PostgreSQL with pgvector and HNSW index** | Separate vector database (e.g. Pinecone/Milvus) | Single database to run, back up, and maintain transactional consistency; measured recall against exact search. |
15: | **D-09** | 2026-10-18 | **8-character codes (40 bits, Crockford-like Base32), HMAC-stored, 5 attempts, 48h expiry** | 6-digit numeric codes | Negligible brute-force collision probability (~4.5 × 10⁻¹²) for identical friction at the desk. |
16: | **D-10** | 2026-10-18 | **Server-side revocable sessions with CSRF tokens** | Stateless JWTs | Instant revocation on logout or account deletion; protection against XSS token theft. |
17: | **D-11** | 2026-10-18 | **Synthetic benchmark with consented real-photo and human-text subsets** | Live student user data | Respects student privacy and consent while enabling reproducible scientific benchmarking. |
18: | **D-12** | 2026-10-18 | **Development-only tuning with frozen configuration** | Tuning on all data | Prevents data leakage; guarantees test set reporting is honest and unbiased. |
19: | **D-13** | 2026-10-18 | **Bootstrap confidence intervals and paired bootstrap testing** | Single-point metrics | Quantifies whether performance differences over baselines are statistically significant. |
20: | **D-14** | 2026-10-18 | **Append-only audit table enforced by DB trigger/privileges** | Application-level logging | Audit rows must be immutable and tamper-evident even if application logic is compromised. |
21: | **D-15** | 2026-10-18 | **Transactional outbox pattern for jobs and notifications** | External message broker (RabbitMQ/Kafka) | Guarantees atomic consistency with database state changes using `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. |
22: | **D-16** | 2026-10-18 | **Credentials over TLS beyond localhost** | Plain HTTP on intranet | Prevents credential and session sniffing over local campus Wi-Fi networks. |
23: | **D-17** | 2026-10-18 | **Email-only identity with campus domain restriction** | Collecting phone numbers or student IDs | Adheres to strict data minimization principles. |

29: def validate_image_file(content: bytes) -> tuple[str, str]:
30:     """AC-31 & AC-32: Validate file content type by magic bytes and guard pixel dimensions."""
31:     # 1. Size guard
32:     if len(content) > MAX_IMAGE_SIZE_BYTES:
33:         raise HTTPException(
34:             status_code=status.HTTP_413_CONTENT_TOO_LARGE,
35:             detail={"code": "image_too_large", "message": "Image size exceeds 5 MB limit."},
36:         )
37: 
38:     # 2. Magic byte inspection (AC-31)
39:     mime: str
40:     ext: str
41:     if content.startswith(b"\xff\xd8\xff"):
42:         mime = "image/jpeg"
43:         ext = ".jpg"
44:     elif content.startswith(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"):
45:         mime = "image/png"
46:         ext = ".png"
47:     elif content.startswith(b"RIFF") and len(content) >= 12 and content[8:12] == b"WEBP":
48:         mime = "image/webp"
49:         ext = ".webp"
50:     else:
51:         # SVG, GIF, text, executable, etc.
52:         raise HTTPException(
53:             status_code=status.HTTP_415_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE,
54:             detail={
55:                 "code": "unsupported_media_type",
56:                 "message": "Only JPEG, PNG, and WebP images are accepted.",
57:             },
58:         )
59: 
60:     # 3. Dimension guard before decoding raster (AC-32)
61:     try:
62:         with Image.open(BytesIO(content)) as img:
63:             w, h = img.size
64:             if w > MAX_DIMENSION or h > MAX_DIMENSION:
65:                 raise HTTPException(
66:                     status_code=status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
67:                     detail={
68:                         "code": "image_too_large",
69:                         "message": f"Image dimensions {w}x{h} exceed 6,000x6,000 maximum.",
70:                     },
71:                 )
72:     except HTTPException:
73:         raise
74:     except Exception as exc:
75:         raise HTTPException(
76:             status_code=status.HTTP_415_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE,
77:             detail={"code": "corrupted_image", "message": "Failed to decode image."},
78:         ) from exc
79: 
80:     return mime, ext
81:

+## Step 15: Stretch Modules — Automated Privacy Blurring in the Photo Pipeline (Spec Section 19)
+
+* **What was built:**
+  * **Pure Domain Privacy Redaction (`backend/app/domain/privacy_blur.py`):**
+    * Implemented zero-framework, deterministic Gaussian image smoothing for target bounding boxes (`(x, y, width, height)`).
+    * Coordinate clamping logic preventing index errors on out-of-bounds inputs.
+  * **Photo Pipeline Integration (`backend/app/services/photo.py`):**
+    * Updated `process_and_save_photo` to accept optional `privacy_regions` to redact human faces, license plates, and student ID badges before permanent disk storage and thumbnail rendering.
+  * **Test Suite (`backend/tests/test_step15_privacy_blurring.py`):**
+    * 5 automated tests verifying bounding box pixel smoothing, preservation of unmasked regions, luminance variance reduction, and end-to-end file persistence.
+  * **Decisions Log Updates:**
+    * Logged decision **D-18** in [`DECISIONS.md`](file:///c:/Users/abhir/OneDrive/Desktop/AIDS/Campus%20lost%20and%20found/DECISIONS.md) and [`spec.md`](file:///c:/Users/abhir/OneDrive/Desktop/AIDS/Campus%20lost%20and%20found/spec.md).
+* **Why it is designed that way:**
+  * **Privacy by Design:** Bystanders and personal identification details (faces, car license plates, university badges) inadvertently captured in lost/found photographs must never be permanently saved or exposed publicly. Blurring these bounding boxes before writing bytes to disk guarantees zero forensic retrieval of unredacted biometric or vehicular markers.
+  * **Offline Pure Domain Execution:** Running redaction locally using PIL Gaussian filters maintains strict air-gapped compliance (**AC-139**) and avoids sending sensitive student media to third-party cloud vision APIs.
+* **One thing that could go wrong:**
+  * **Degraded Perceptual Hashing if Whole Image Blurred:** Blurring overly broad regions could destroy perceptual image features needed for duplicate detection (`dHash`) or visual CLIP matching. Mitigated by applying blur strictly to isolated bounding boxes while preserving the surrounding item context.
+* **Quiz Questions (for viva preparation):**
+  1. *Why should biometric face and license plate redaction occur before saving images to disk rather than dynamically blurring them on the client?*
+  2. *How does Gaussian smoothing inside a localized bounding box reduce edge variance while preserving overall image layout and perceptual dHash stability?*
+  3. *Why must the privacy blurring logic reside in the pure domain layer without external cloud computer vision dependencies?*

1: # Deployment Guide: Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network
2: 
3: This guide explains how to deploy and access the **Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network** across different environments, from instant public URLs to permanent production cloud hosting.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 1. Instant Live Tunnel (Active Now)
8: 
9: Your local Compose stack has been tunneled via Cloudflare Tunnel to provide an immediate, secure public HTTPS URL:
10: 
11: * **Live Public URL:** [`https://capable-telling-accordance-href.trycloudflare.com`](https://capable-telling-accordance-href.trycloudflare.com)
12: * **API Health Check:** [`https://capable-telling-accordance-href.trycloudflare.com/api/health`](https://capable-telling-accordance-href.trycloudflare.com/api/health)
13: 
14: ### Running or Restarting the Tunnel
15: To regenerate or restart the tunnel at any time:
16: ```bash
17: ~/.local/bin/cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080
18: ```
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 2. Permanent Cloud Deployment Options
23: 
24: ### Option A: Railway / Render (Containerized)
25: 1. Fork or push this repository to GitHub.
26: 2. In [Railway.app](https://railway.app) or [Render.com](https://render.com), click **New Project** -> **Deploy from GitHub repo**.
27: 3. Railway automatically detects `docker-compose.yml` or you can provision:
28:    - **PostgreSQL Database** with `pgvector` extension enabled (`CREATE EXTENSION vector;`).
29:    - **Backend Web Service**: Root directory `backend`, build command `Dockerfile`.
30:    - **Frontend Web Service**: Root directory `frontend`, build command `Dockerfile`.
31: 4. Configure environment variables in the dashboard:
32:    ```env
33:    ENVIRONMENT=production
34:    SECRET_KEY=<generate_secure_random_hex_32_bytes>
35:    ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=campus.edu,student.campus.edu
36:    DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://<user>:<password>@<db-host>:5432/<dbname>
37:    ```
38: 
39: ### Option B: VPS (DigitalOcean, AWS EC2, Hetzner, Linode)
40: 1. Provision an Ubuntu 24.04 LTS instance with Docker and Docker Compose installed.
41: 2. Clone your repository:
42:    ```bash
43:    git clone <repo_url> /opt/campus-lost-and-found
44:    cd /opt/campus-lost-and-found
45:    ```
46: 3. Configure your production environment:
47:    ```bash
48:    cp .env.example .env
49:    # Edit .env with your domain name and production secret keys
50:    ```
51: 4. Build and start the production stack:
52:    ```bash
53:    docker compose up -d --build
54:    docker compose exec -T backend alembic upgrade head
55:    docker compose exec -T backend python -m app.seed
56:    ```
57: 5. Set up TLS using Caddy or Nginx with Let's Encrypt for automatic HTTPS renewals on your custom campus domain.
58: 
59: ---
60:

63: When visiting the live link, you can test the application using the pre-seeded accounts:

### How to Access & Use Sign In

1. **Open the live application:**
   👉 **[https://capable-telling-accordance-href.trycloudflare.com](https://capable-telling-accordance-href.trycloudflare.com)**

2. **Locate the button:**
   - Look at the top-right corner of the page for the button:
   - **`🔑 Sign In / Demo Accounts`**

3. **Click it to open the Sign In Modal:**
   The modal provides two ways to log in:
   
   - **One-Click Instant Demo Roles (Fastest):**
     Click any of the 4 role buttons to immediately sign in without typing:
     - 🎓 **Alice (Student):** `student1@campus.edu` *(Lost item workflow & matching)*
     - 🔍 **Bob (Student):** `student2@campus.edu` *(Found item workflow & claims)*
     - 🛡️ **Staff Moderator:** `moderator@campus.edu` *(Moderation review queue & handover verification)*
     - ⚙️ **Campus Admin:** `admin@campus.edu` *(System administration, audit logs & location management)*
   
   - **Manual Email & Password:**
     Enter any valid campus domain email (`@campus.edu`) and password.

4. **Logged-In State:**
   - Once signed in, the top-right header updates to show your active role badge (e.g. `STUDENT`, `MODERATOR`, `ADMIN`), your email address, and a **`Sign Out`** button.

3: **Version:** 1.0 (draft, based on *Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network: Project Blueprint*)
4: **Last updated:** 2026-10-18

11: ## 1. Overview
12: 
13: A full-stack web application where campus users report lost and found belongings, the system suggests likely matches using text, photos, campus location and time, and campus staff verify claims and complete handovers with a one-time code. AI suggestions are **advice for humans**: no score ever approves a claim or changes a status.
14: 
15: The project has two halves of equal weight. The **product** half is a trustworthy workflow: privacy-aware public listings, evidence-based claims, moderator review, expiring single-use handover codes, an audit trail, and retention rules. The **research** half asks a measurable question: *does combining text, image, location and time signals retrieve lost items better than keyword search?* It is answered on a controlled benchmark with proper splits, confidence intervals and ablations.
16: 
17: The blueprint itself notes that AI-assisted lost-and-found systems already exist. This project does not claim a novel idea. Its contribution is a careful, secure, explainable campus workflow and an honestly measured comparison.
18: 
19: ### Aim
20: 
21: Build a secure, campus-aware lost-and-found platform with explainable multimodal matching, a verified claim and handover process, and a reproducible evaluation of hybrid retrieval against keyword and single-signal baselines, deployed as a service you can open in a browser on your computer or local network.

56: ## 2. Goals, Scope and Non-Goals
57: 
58: **Goals**
59: 1. Accounts with roles (user, moderator, admin) and campus-email verification.
60: 2. A hierarchical campus location model that tolerates approximate locations.
61: 3. Lost and found reports with a safe photo pipeline and a defined lifecycle.
62: 4. Searchable listings that never expose private details.
63: 5. Background embedding jobs and a hybrid matching engine with explanations.
64: 6. Notifications (in-app and email) through a reliable outbox.
65: 7. Claims, moderator review, and one-time handover codes.
66: 8. An append-only audit log, retention rules, and data export and deletion.
67: 9. An analytics dashboard.
68: 10. A reproducible evaluation of keyword, text, image and hybrid retrieval.
69: 11. A tested, documented, deployed system.
70: 
71: **Non-goals (v1)**
72: - Campus single sign-on, mobile apps, push notifications, or SMS.
73: - Automatic ownership decisions, or any AI action without human review.
74: - GPS tracking or precise indoor positioning.
75: - Facial recognition. Photos are never used to identify people.
76: - Evidence that the system improves real-world recovery rates (only a pilot could show that; the benchmark does not).
77: 
78: **Stretch** (only after every required criterion passes): a SigLIP-family model comparison, multilingual text, face and number-plate blurring in photos, learning from dismissals, campus SSO, and a digest email.

209: ### 6.3 Location and time scores
210: 
211: **Location score** by the relationship between the two locations in the tree:
212: 
213: | Relationship | Score |
214: | --- | --- |
215: | Identical | 1.0 |
216: | One is an ancestor of the other | 0.8 |
217: | Share a floor or an area (lowest common ancestor is a floor or an area) | 0.7 |
218: | Share a building only | 0.6 |
219: | Different buildings that are adjacent | 0.5 |
220: | Same campus, not adjacent | 0.2 |
221: | Different campuses | 0.0 |
222: | A location is missing | `null` |
223: 
224: **Time score** compares the two windows. If they overlap, the score is 1. Otherwise let `gap` be the hours between them: if the found window is after the lost window, `score = exp(−gap / 48)`; if it is before, `score = exp(−gap / 6)`. The asymmetry reflects that a finder cannot find something before it was lost, apart from imprecise reporting.
225: 
226: ### 6.4 Hybrid score
227: 
228: `score = Σ wᵢ sᵢ / Σ wᵢ`, summed **only over signals that are not `null`**. Initial weights: text 0.40, image 0.35, location 0.15, time 0.10. Missing signals are excluded, never treated as zero. Each stored candidate records its weights version. Bins: at least 0.75 `high`, at least 0.55 `medium`, otherwise `low`. A match notification is sent only for a score of at least 0.65 ranked in the top 3. Weights and thresholds are tuned on the development set only (section 7).
229: 
230: ### 6.5 Candidates and retrieval
231: 
232: A candidate pair is a lost report and a found report where both are `open`, the reporters differ, the pair has not been dismissed, and the found time lies between 6 hours before the lost window starts and 30 days after it ends. Retrieval uses the HNSW index to fetch the nearest neighbours by text and by image, merges them with the location and time candidates, scores them all, and returns the top K (default 10). New reports trigger scoring in both directions, and each (lost, found, model version, weights version) is scored once. Ties break by the older found report, then by ID.
233:

1: import uuid
2: from dataclasses import dataclass
3: from typing import Literal
4: 
5: LocationKind = Literal["campus", "building", "floor", "room", "area"]
6: 
7: 
8: @dataclass(frozen=True)
9: class LocationNode:
10:     id: uuid.UUID
11:     name: str
12:     kind: LocationKind
13:     parent: "LocationNode | None" = None
14: 
15: 
16: def _get_ancestor_chain(node: LocationNode) -> list[LocationNode]:
17:     """Return the chain of nodes from the current node up to the root."""
18:     chain: list[LocationNode] = []
19:     curr: LocationNode | None = node
20:     while curr is not None:
21:         chain.append(curr)
22:         curr = curr.parent
23:     return chain
24: 
25: 
26: def calculate_location_score(
27:     loc_a: LocationNode | None,
28:     loc_b: LocationNode | None,
29:     adjacency_set: set[tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID]] | None = None,
30: ) -> float | None:
31:     """[LEARN] Pure domain location scoring function per Spec 6.3 and AC-18.
32: 
33:     Scores the relationship between two locations in a campus tree:
34:     - 1.0: Identical location
35:     - 0.8: One is an ancestor of the other
36:     - 0.7: Share a floor or an area (LCA is floor or area)
37:     - 0.6: Share a building only (LCA is building)
38:     - 0.5: Different buildings that are adjacent
39:     - 0.2: Same campus, not adjacent
40:     - 0.0: Different campuses
41:     - None (null): Either location is missing
42:     """
43:     if loc_a is None or loc_b is None:
44:         return None
45: 
46:     # 1. Identical location
47:     if loc_a.id == loc_b.id:
48:         return 1.0
49: 
50:     chain_a = _get_ancestor_chain(loc_a)
51:     chain_b = _get_ancestor_chain(loc_b)
52: 
53:     # 2. One is an ancestor of the other
54:     ancestor_ids_a = {node.id for node in chain_a[1:]}
55:     ancestor_ids_b = {node.id for node in chain_b[1:]}
56: 
57:     if loc_a.id in ancestor_ids_b or loc_b.id in ancestor_ids_a:

92:         return 0.2

94:     return 0.0

ASSISTANT (ANTIGRAVITY) [Step 3444]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
In the **Smart Campus Lost-and-Found Network**, campuses are distinguished across three architectural layers:

---

### 1. Hierarchical Location Tree (Spatial Topology)
Every location in the database ([`campus_locations`](file:///c:/Users/abhir/OneDrive/Desktop/AIDS/Campus%20lost%20and%20found/backend/app/models/location.py)) is part of a strict parent-child tree:
```
Campus (Root)
 └── Building (e.g., Library, Science Block)
      └── Floor / Area (e.g., Floor 2, Cafeteria)
           └── Room (e.g., Lab 101, Reading Room)
```
* **Different Campuses:** Have completely different root nodes (e.g., `Main Campus` vs. `Downtown Campus` vs. `Health Sciences Campus`). They share no common ancestor in the tree.
* **Building Adjacency:** Buildings on the same campus can have defined physical walking paths via the `location_adjacency` table. Cross-campus buildings never share physical adjacency.

---

### 2. AI Matching & Proximity Scoring
When a student reports a lost item, the multimodal AI matcher calculates the **spatial similarity score** ([`calculate_location_score`](file:///c:/Users/abhir/OneDrive/Desktop/AIDS/Campus%20lost%20and%20found/backend/app/domain/location.py#L26-L95)) based on tree distance:

| Location Relationship | Location Score | Effect on Matching |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Identical spot** (e.g. same room) | **`1.0`** | Maximum match boost |
| **Same floor / area** | **`0.7`** | Strong match boost |
| **Same building** | **`0.6`** | Moderate match boost |
| **Adjacent buildings** (same campus) | **`0.5`** | Likely candidate |
| **Same campus**, non-adjacent | **`0.2`** | Minor spatial signal |
| **Different campuses** | **`0.0`** | **Zero location score** (strongly suppresses cross-campus false positives) |

> **Key Rule:** An item lost at one campus and found at another receives a `0.0` location score, preventing students from receiving irrelevant recommendations from distant campuses.

---

### 3. Institutional Authentication Boundaries
* **Email Domain Filtering:** Each deployment configures `ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS` (e.g., `@campus.edu`, `@student.campus.edu`). Different universities or collegiate systems cannot register or view internal listings without an approved institutional identity.
* **Physical Handover Desks:** Handover desks operate at specific physical buildings on that campus. Single-use 8-character verification codes must be presented in person at the local campus desk to complete a claim.
